title: Ireland – Construction work – 14 Tullyglass Hill
description: Corlann Clare invites tenders from suitably experienced building contractors for the extension and refurbishment of an existing single-storey dwelling at 14 Tullyglass Hill, Shannon, Co. Clare, V14 KH42. The works comprise a new single-storey extension of approximately 45 m² and the full refurbishment and upgrade of the existing house. The main elements are: • Demolition and strip-out: demolition of the existing lean-to structure on the east side; removal of the glazed courtyard roof, chimney stack, oil boiler and oil tank; full internal strip-out of finishes, ceilings, fittings, sanitaryware, and heating, plumbing and electrical installations. • New extension: 225 mm solid blockwork on a raft foundation to the Structural Engineer's design, with a certified external wall insulation and render system, and an insulated warm-deck flat roof. • Existing house: replacement of all windows and external doors; new and altered openings with steel beams and lintels; removal and alteration of internal walls; upgrade of all existing flat roofs to warm-deck construction; a new solid warm-deck roof with rooflights over the courtyard; rebuilt rooflight upstand walls; render repairs and redecoration; new fascias, gutters and downpipes. • Internal fit-out: new internal layout including WC and shower rooms, a widened stair and a new platform lift; FD30 fire door sets with closers and electromagnetic hold-open devices; fire-rated glazing; automatic opening smoke vents linked to a fire alarm system; [new heating, ventilation and electrical installations to the Specification]. • External works: widened entrance and tarmac driveway; new gently sloped footpaths and a level landing at a relocated main entrance on the west elevation; new and rebuilt retaining walls; new patio; replacement of asewer lines, installation of new manholes; new surface water drainage; tree removal and reinstatement of landscaping.

title: U006--VR&E Self-Employment Services RFI
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) SUBJECT Exploring the Feasibility of VA Partnering with Industry to Ready Disabled Veterans for Self-Employment (i.e., entrepreneurship; small business ownership) 1.0 INTRODUCTION The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Benefits Administration (VBA), is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) for Veteran Readiness & Employment (VR&E) Self-Employment Services. The information provided in response to this request may be used by VBA in developing its acquisition strategy and refining the Performance Work Statement (PWS). THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION. The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this RFI or otherwise pay for the information requested. Responses will be treated as information only and not as a proposal. There is no obligation for the Government to acquire any products or services described in this RFI. In accordance with the Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR) Subpart 15.101(c)(2), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. 2.0 BACKGROUND VBA s VR&E Service, pursuant to Title 38 United States Code Chapter 31 (see Section 3100), provides to eligible Veterans with compensable service-connected disabilities all services and assistance necessary to enable them to achieve maximum independence in daily living and, to the maximum extent feasible, to become employable and to obtain and maintain suitable employment. After achieving the degree of rehabilitation needed to become suitably employed, VR&E is expected to assist Veterans in the pursuit of suitable employment. One such avenue through which VR&E assists is utilizing VR&E s Self-Employment Track, which is intended to assist eligible Veterans in achieving their vocational goals in entrepreneurship and business ownership. Services include the following: Developing and strengthening a business plan Training in small-business operations, marketing, finances, etc. Assessing the feasibility of implementing such a business plan Obtaining (through loans or grants) the resources necessary to implement a business plan and incorporate the business such as securing loans Purchasing of equipment, acquiring initial stocks and supplies, etc. Specialized expertise and/or support to assist Veterans interested in self-employment includes, but is not limited to, knowledge of local/state/federal laws associated with starting a business;� market research/analysis both from the perspective of assessing viability of the prospective business in the job market and through the lens of purchasing subject matter expertise and purchasing equipment/supplies; and� potential screening or other assessment tools for specialized job markets (i.e. ability to run background checks and/or credit checks to assess criminal history, driving records, substance use/abuse, financial/credit/tax history, education, etc.). Further, VA recognizes that achieving successful self-employment outcomes often requires specialized expertise beyond traditional vocational rehabilitation services. Veterans pursuing entrepreneurship may need support with business planning, feasibility analysis, market research, financial literacy, regulatory compliance, business startup requirements, mentorship, and access to entrepreneurial networks and resources. Self-employment cases frequently involve complex business considerations that require specialized knowledge, individualized assessments, and coordination with public and private sector resources. Veterans may require assistance evaluating business viability, developing comprehensive business plans, understanding applicable licensing and regulatory requirements, conducting market and financial analyses, identifying startup resource needs, and building the skills necessary to successfully operate a small business. These needs often require tailored, ongoing guidance throughout the planning and launch process. VA is seeking information on how experienced industry partners can supplement existing VR&E services by providing subject matter expertise, structured entrepreneurial training, business feasibility assessments, market research capabilities, business financial planning and analysis (i.e., financial projections, startup cost estimates, cash flow planning, and capital requirements), and access to established business support networks. Such services may help Veterans make informed business decisions, evaluate and strengthen the viability of proposed business ventures, develop stronger business plans, and access the expertise and resources needed to successfully launch and sustain a small business. Accordingly, VA requests information from organizations with demonstrated experience providing entrepreneur and small business support services, including business advisory services, training, business feasibility and market assessments, entrepreneurial training, startup incubation, financial planning, and other related support services. The goal is to identify potential partnership approaches that can enhance VA's ability to assist Veterans with service-connected disabilities in evaluating business concepts, developing viable business plans, preparing for business ownership, and successfully launching and sustaining small businesses 3.0 INFORMATION SOUGHT The Government is seeking the following information from vendors responding to this RFI: Organization and Contact Information, specifically: Name of Organization Addresses for Primary Locations of Operation Points of Contact (available for follow-up discussions) Phone Numbers and Email Addresses for Points of Contact Business Size and Socioeconomic Status Answers to List of Questions (See Section 5.0 of this RFI) Past Performance (if applicable) describing how your organization: has supported entrepreneurs in exploring, planning, and starting small business enterprises prepared entrepreneurs for operating small business enterprises with training, apprenticeships, mentorships, and similar educational ventures 4.0 SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS Please submit responses to the Contracting Officer, Edward Bradford, via email Edward.Bradford@va.gov no later than November 25, 2026. Responses shall not exceed 10 pages total and shall be prepared in Times New Roman, 12-point font, with 1-inch margins. 5.0 LIST OF QUESTIONS Please provide information regarding proposed joint ventures, teaming arrangements, or strategic alliances you believe would be beneficial in supporting the needs of Veterans pursuing self-employment outlined in the background section of this document. Please describe your organization s expertise in providing business planning, self-employment, entrepreneurship, small business operations, and startup incubation services. Please describe how your organization would prepare for and respond to referrals issued by VR&E, specifically the timelines for contacting Veterans participating in the Self-Employment Track and the type of services your organization would provide throughout the engagement. Please describe your organization s service delivery model, including how services would be documented and how progress, milestones, and outcomes would be communicated to VA. On average, how many full-time equivalent (FTE) business consultants, entrepreneurship specialists, or small business advisors are employed by your company? How long has your company been providing self-employment, entrepreneurship development, small business consulting, or related business advisory services? Please provide the qualifications, certifications, or specialized training your business consultants possess related to entrepreneurship? Please describe your experience developing business plans, feasibility studies, and financial projections. description: PRE-SOLICITATION SYNOPSIS NOTICE ONLY: THE SOLICITATION WILL BE AVAILABLE ON OR ABOUT NOVEMBER 30, 2026 AT HTTPS://SAM.GOV/. THE SOLICITATION NUMBER IS N6945027R0008, FOR THE DESIGN-BID-BUILD (DBB) CONSTRUCTION PROJECT P233 AIR TRAFFIC CONTROL TOWER AND FLIGHT SIMULATOR TRAINING FACILITY AT KEESLER AIR FORCE BASE (AFB), BILOXI, MISSISSIPPI PROJECT TITLE: DESIGN BID BUILD (DBB) CONSTRUCTION PROJECT, P233 AIR TRAFFIC CONTROL TOWER AND FLIGHT SIMULATOR TRAINING FACILITY AT KEESLER AIR FORCE BASE (AFB), BILOXI, MISSISSIPPI PSC: Y1BA (Construction of Air Traffic Control Towers) NAICS: 236220 � Commercial and Institutional Building Construction THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS OR AN INVITATION FOR BID. NO CONTRACT WILL BE AWARDED FROM THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO REIMBURSEMENT WILL BE MADE FOR ANY COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH PROVIDING INFORMATION IN RESPONSE TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT OR ANY FOLLOW-UP INFORMATION REQUESTS. No telephone calls will be accepted requesting a bid package or solicitation. There is no bid package or solicitation currently available. In order to protect the procurement integrity of any future procurement that may arise from this announcement, information regarding the technical point of contact will not be given and no appointments for presentations will be made. Description: This acquisition may result in the award of a Design Bid Build (DBB) Firm Fixed Price (FFP) Construction contract of an Air Traffic Control Tower and Flight Simulator Training Facility at Keesler AFB, Mississippi. This project will construct a new Air Traffic Control Tower and adjacent Flight Simulator Facility. Project includes all utilities, site improvements, pavements, elevator, backup generator, and all necessary work for a complete and usable facility. Project will comply with Department of Defense Antiterrorism/Force Protection requirements per Unified Facilities Criteria 4-010-01 and Unified Facilities Criteria 3-600-01. A Bid Option is included for the demolition of Buildings 4209 and 4230, to include site grading and the installation of a security fence. Demolition in this bid option to only occur after the new Air Traffic Control Tower is complete. The estimated Period of Performance is 1,219 calendar days. The best value continuum source selection process to be used for this acquisition is the Best Value Tradeoff process as described in FAR 15.103-1. The Best Value Tradeoff process is appropriate and permits evaluation of proposals based on price competition, technical merit, confidence assessment and other factors; permits impartial and comprehensive evaluation of offeror proposals; permits discussions if necessary; and ensures selection of the source whose performance provides the best value to the Government. A sources sought notice was posted to sam.gov on October 27, 2026, requesting small business industry interest and capability statements. Based on responses from the notice it was determined that the requirement should be issued as Full and Open competition. The solicitation will be a negotiated DBB acquisition. Proposals will be solicited in a one-phase submission for a single solicitation. The solicitation will utilize source selection procedures, which require offerors to submit a technical proposal, past performance and experience information, and a price proposal for evaluation by the Government. Award will be made to the offeror whose total price and technical proposal offers the best value to the Government. Competition Requirements: Unrestricted basis, under full and open competition. Procurement Method: FAR Part 15, Contracting by Negotiation. Type of Contract: Firm-Fixed Price The NAICS code for this construction solicitation is 236220 with a size standard of $45,000,000. Project Magnitude is between $20,000,000 and $50,000,000. This is a new procurement. It does not replace an existing contract. No prior contract information exists. A Site Visit will be held for those offerors who choose to participate (exact date and time will be specified in the solicitation). Proposals will be due no earlier than 30 days after the solicitation is released (exact date and time will be specified in the solicitation). This will be an electronic solicitation, which can be downloaded from Sam.gov Opportunities at https://sam.gov/. The solicitation will be available at this site no earlier than 15 days after this pre-solicitation notice is posted. Offerors are responsible for checking the Sam.gov website for the solicitation and any subsequent amendments that may be issued. NO CONTRACT AWARD WILL BE MADE TO ANY CONTRACTOR THAT IS NOT REGISTERED OR IN THE PROCESS OF REGISTERING WITH THE SYSTEM FOR AWARD MANAGEMENT (SAM). title: APN-CONSTRUCTION MANAGEMENT SERVICES, MAINLAND BC INFRASTRUCTURE MODERNIZATION
description: ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE CONSTRUCTION MANAGEMENT SERVICES FOR MAINLAND BRITISH COLUMBIA INFRASTRUCTURE MODERNIZATION PROGRAM (with security requirements) 1. PURPOSE OF THIS ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals. In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform contractors of an upcoming contract opportunity at Chilliwack, British Columbia and various range and training areas across Mainland BC. The purpose of this APN is to allow contractors to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process. This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested contractors to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable). Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process. Please note that this project may include Indigenous businesses participation component in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB). 2. DESCRIPTION OF THE PROJECT AND SERVICES It is anticipated that the following solicitation will proceed as noted in the table below. This is conditional on the contract receiving approval to proceed from DND. APN: 87908 Approximate Estimate: $125,000,000 Anticipated Posting: Winter 2027 Description: The Infrastructure Modernization Program at Chilliwack, British Columbia and various range and training areas across Mainland BC is focused on both recapitalization of existing assets and the development of new infrastructure and facilities where required. As part of this project, the Department of National Defence (DND) wishes to proceed with the renewal of systems which include civil, architectural, mechanical, electrical, and environmental elements to bring the assets to meet current and projected future requirements. This program will include planned phased work packages for implementation over ten (10) years while maintaining operations across Mainland BC. The purpose of this project is to retain the services of a contractor to provide construction management services of pre-construction and construction phases.  Major construction services are expected to include activities such as interior/exterior demolition in the presence of hazardous materials, interior renovations, exterior envelope work, electrical, mechanical, civil, structural and new infrastructure. 3. CONTRACT AWARD AND ANTICIPATED SECURITY REQUIREMENTS To be eligible for contract award, a proponent will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents. The anticipated security clearance level for this contract is Designated Organization Screening (DOS). 4. Industrial Security Program Sponsorship Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing contractors early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, contractors that intend to submit a proposal for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP. Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential proponents with their respective security clearance sponsorship process. To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements. In their sponsorship request application to DCC, contractors are asked to quote the following information, among other things: Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number, as identified in Section 2 of this APN; and Level of clearance requested to be sponsored, as identified in Section 3 of this APN. 5. Sponsorship Process Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the contractors to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages. Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a contractor: has started the sponsorship process prior to the solicitation being advertised on MERX, has met all the material requirements of the sponsorship request package prior to the closing date indicated in the solicitation, and has submitted a proposal.   DCC will send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP). Note – Contractors that do not submit a proposal will not be able to attain clearance through this sponsorship process. Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the proponent regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. At such time, the proponent will need to promptly cooperate with CSP to ensure that the process is completed as soon as possible. 6. Questions Any questions pertaining to the sponsoring process through the ISP can be addressed to: Telephone Number: (613) 998-8974; or Email address: ISP.Sponsorship@dcc-cdc.gc.ca Any questions relating to this Advance Procurement Notice can be addressed to: Theresa Tran Coordinator, Contract Services Defence Construction Canada (604) 832 8373 theresa.tran@dcc-cdc.gc.ca 7. Disclaimer DCC is only providing assistance, at its entire discretion, for the above stated sponsorship process  and does not provide any representations  or guarantees that a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application forwarded by DCC to the CSP will be successful or result in the granting of the requested security clearance(s) by the CSP. At all times, the processing of a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application is subject to the respective terms, conditions, and timelines of DCC’s ISP sponsorship process and the CSP security clearance granting process. By applying to either of the aforementioned processes, the proponent agrees to bear any fees and risks associated with: (i) the completeness or accuracy, or lack thereof, of its application or related documents submitted under or in connection with either said processes, and (ii) the timeliness, or lack thereof, of any processing or granting of security clearance(s) under or in connection with either said processes. Notwithstanding anything else stated above, DCC shall in no event be liable to the proponent for any direct, indirect, incidental, special, consequential, punitive or exemplary damages arising out or in connection with the above stated sponsorship process.Bidding and Documents are available on http://www.merx.com. Fees may apply; See https://www.merx.com/public/pricing for more information.

title: FMC Carswell 2 QTR FY27 Halal Meal Solicitation
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products prepared in accordance with the format in Revolutionary FAR Overhaul FAR Subpart 12.2, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. The solicitation number is 15B50527Q00000007 and is issued as a Request for Quote (RFQ). This Solicitation is for 2nd Qtr. FY27 Halal Meals Solicitation. The solicitation document, incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Revolutionary FAR Overhaul issuance date May 2, 2025. This solicitation is issued as Total small business set-aside. The associated North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 311999 with a small business size standard of 700.00 employees. FOB Destination shall be to: FMC Carswell Food Service Department 1200 Meandering Road, Fort Worth, Texas 76114. Items will be awarded individually. More than one item may be awarded to one offeror/contractor. Award will be given to the offeror whose bid/quote conforms to the requirements and is determined to provide the best value to the Government. The following are the evaluation factors that will be used to evaluate each offeror are price, past performance and best value (conformity to applicable and requested specifications). Past performance and specification conformity are significantly as important as price. Quotes shall be accepted up to 4 decimal places. Religious Certification Requirements for Meals Items offered on this bid must be certified Halal. Please read definitions below for requirement of each certification. Certified Halal items will be certified by a Halal Certification Agency, to meet the following requirements: With no pork or pork by-products; No traces of alcohol, or additives containing alcohol, including sugar alcohols; No gelatin derived from haram sources; No animal shortening derived from haram sources; No other mind-altering substances derived from haram sources; No forbidden enzymes derived from haram sources; No emulsifiers that are derived from haram sources; That has no exposure to haram foods or ingredients through cross contact. Quality assurance mechanisms to ensure no cross contact with haram food or ingredients. The animal from which the meat comes: Must be lawful to consume in Islamic Law. Cannot have died of cause other than proper slaughtering in accordance with Islam; The live animal must be slaughtered: By hand with an extremely sharp knife so that the animal suffers minimally; Intentionally slaughtered by a horizontal cut at the throat of the animal (below is laryngeal prominence), so that three of the four vessels are severed in one cut; By a practicing sane adult Muslim who is knowledgeable of the Islamic slaughtering procedures. The slaughterer must believe in all the essential matters of the Islamic faith. The slaughterer must recite Bismillah (In the Name of Allah) before the slaughter of each animal, and in a manner prescribed by Islamic law. The Halal slaughtered carcasses should be stamped and labeled as �Halal' Quoters will include a letter of certification from the religious certification agency dated no more than 11 months from the date of the quote provided. General Meal Specifications - Items 1 through 12 1) The tray for all meals will be: a) Made with non-metallic packaging that allows microwave and conventional oven heating and be heat sealed directly to the tray with clear plastic and wrapped with a separate sealed clear plastic wrapper which encloses the entire tray. b) A three-compartment tray with a large compartment of 21 fluid ounces and two compartments of 6 fluid ounces each. 2) All Meals will contain the food products per the individual product specification including the stated volume and/or weight of item as listed. 3) No substitutions may be made to the meats, vegetables, starches, sauces or preparation methods. 4) Meals (items 1 through 12) may be quoted as frozen and/or shelf stable products. Pricing must be identifiable as either frozen or shelf stable. 5) Each individual meal must be marked with the certification symbol from the religious certification agency. 6) Heating directions must be provided for various wattage microwaves or oven heating including recommended method. 7) Mixed Vegetables will contain carrots, corn, peas, green beans, and lima beans with: a) Not more than 40 percent by weight carrots. b) Not more than 40 percent by weight corn (sweet, golden or yellow, whole kernel com). c) Not more than 40 percent by weight green peas. 8) Peas and Carrots will contain: a) Not more than 40 percent by weight carrots. b) Not more than 40 percent by weight green peas. 9) Mashed Potatoes will be made with commercially prepared potato flakes without peel, adding only water according to the manufacturers� preparation instructions; or fresh potatoes prepared using only water and spices with only the amount of binder which will ensure the product does separate in processing. No extenders of any type are allowed. 10) Tomato Sauce will be commercially prepared or crushed and/or pureed tomatoes, tomato paste and spices using only the amount of binder required to ensure the product does not separate during processing. DELIVERY REQUIREMENTS/INSTRUCTIONS: Product(s) must meet Certified Menu Specifications; must have a legible expiration date that is at least 6 months past date delivered or will not be accepted All boxes/cases must be properly labeled (no write on labels or crossed out labels) All deliveries must be palletized unless prior arrangements were agreed to by warehouse staff. All non-frozen, perishable foods must be delivered between 34 degrees F and 40 degrees F. Any product that indicates prior thawing will be refused. All items must strictly follow the BOP Religious Diet Specifications. Food Service contractors have the responsibility of understanding these specifications. Contractors must obtain a copy of the Religious Diet Specifications prior to quoting. All items will be closely inspected. Some items may require thawing and cooking to determine specification compliance. Receipt of delivery may be conditional for a period of three (3) days to allow for adequate examination and testing. Items that fail to meet specifications will be refused. Items which are conditionally received and found noncompliant must be picked up at the vendors� expense within (2) weeks of noncompliance notification. If the product is not picked up within two (2) weeks, it will be disposed of by warehouse staff. Items that fail to meet specifications will be refused. All items must be dated. Deliveries will be accepted from 7:30 a.m. to 2:00 pm CST, Monday through Fridays, No deliveries on weekends or federal holidays. Delivery is on a first - come, first - serve basis. No delivery appointment is required. For any further delivery queries contact our Warehouse Supervisor at 817-782-4268. Unless otherwise stated within the specification of an item description in Section 2 of SF Form 1449, all dates for frozen food items must be delivered frozen and delivered before the best buy date, sell by date, use by date, best if used by date, or freeze by date on the label. Delivery vehicles should not exceed Gross 49000lbs-Tandem Axle 32000 Lbs. to comply with the bridge weight limit along the delivery route to the warehouse. Please mark all deliveries to reflect: Attn Food Service Department. Payments will be made upon complete delivery and acceptance of the product. Awards will be made via purchase order (EFT). Invoices are to be sent electronically to CRW-BusinessOffice-S@bop.gov. Please read the attached solicitation document in entirety, noting the requested information, specifications, types and packaging sizes as applicable. title: Request for Information (RFI) � Market Research for Ocean Transportation of Hazardous Waste (Guam to CONUS)
description: *** Please be advised that this RFI - Market Research is posted under both NAICS codes 483113 and 483111 to ensure the broadest possible industry dissemination. The postings are identical; interested parties need submit only one response. *** November 3, 2026 Attention Maritime Transportation / Ocean Freight industry partners: Request for Information (RFI) � Market Research for Ocean Transportation of Hazardous Waste (Guam to CONUS) The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) is conducting a market survey to determine the commercial availability and operational capacity of ocean carriers to transport government-generated hazardous waste from the Territory of Guam to permitted facilities in the United States. Pursuant to the Military Cargo Preference Act (10 U.S.C. � 2631) and coastwise trade statutes under 46 U.S.C. Chapter 551, the Government is evaluating the availability of qualified U.S.-flagged vessels, including coastwise-endorsed vessels and U.S.-flagged vessels operating under registry endorsements in accordance with the statutory Guam trade exemption (46 U.S.C. � 12111(b)). This market survey assesses industry capability to meet technical environmental safety standards and required volume throughput, while establishing factual market data regarding whether domestic vessel capacity is sufficient or if alternative statutory authorities, such as the hazardous waste transport exception under 46 U.S.C. � 55105(b) or applicable administrative waiver procedures must be evaluated to ensure mission readiness and regulatory compliance. 1. The current Cargo Description and Operational Requirements for DLA are: a. Cargo Type: Department of War (DoW) Generated Hazardous Waste. The waste streams include a broad range of materials, including: i. RCRA-regulated hazardous waste: Waste exhibiting ignitability (D001), corrosivity (D002), reactivity (D003), or toxicity characteristics, including waste containing lead, chromium, cadmium, mercury, benzene, and other hazardous constituents. ii. Contaminated liquids: Waste fuels, gasoline, solvents, paints, thinners, corrosive liquids, contaminated wastewater, and other petroleum- or chemically contaminated liquids. iii. Used oil and petroleum-related waste: Used lubricating oil, oily water, oil filters, sludge, and petroleum contaminated materials, some of which may be managed as non-RCRA-regulated waste. iv. Batteries: Lithium-ion batteries, lithium-metal batteries, lead-acid batteries, nickel-cadmium batteries, and other spent batteries requiring regulated transportation or disposal. v. Contaminated solids: Paint debris, spent blasting media, contaminated soil, oily rags, absorbents, filters, and other solids contaminated with hazardous substances. vi. Other hazardous materials and waste: Oxidizers, corrosive chemicals, flammable substances, aerosol waste, and compressed gas cylinders, where applicable. The cargo includes both RCRA hazardous waste requiring a Uniform Hazardous Waste Manifest and other regulated or non-hazardous waste streams. Individual shipments vary in composition and may contain materials classified under multiple DOT/IMDG hazard classes, including Classes 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, and 9. b. Waste is generally packaged in approved drums, intermediate bulk containers (IBCs), or other appropriate containers and consolidated into 40-foot shipping containers. Bulk liquid waste may also be transported in ISO tank containers. The applicable waste classifications, quantities, and packaging are identified on the corresponding waste profiles, manifests, and shipping documents. c. Hazard Class/UN Number Required: (See Attached List.) d. Required Weekly Throughput Estimate: 2 Each � (40-Foot Container�s) e. Route: Guam to United States (West Coast) f. Required Shipping Window: Present � Indefinite Interested industry partners are requested to submit a written response to this Request for Information (RFI) within twenty (20) calendar days from the date of publication of this notice. This will enable the Government to thoroughly evaluate commercial market capacity, operational feasibility, and statutory compliance. Submissions should directly address the following required questions: 1. Company Information a. Company Legal Name: b. Company Cage Code: c. Physical Address: d. Website: e. Primary NAICS code: f. Business Size (large / small): g. Any socioeconomic status, if any: 2. Point of Contact a. Name: b. Title: c. Phone: d. Email: 3. Status: Does your company currently operate a Jones Act-compliant vessel scheduled on this route during the specified shipping window? 4. Technical Certification: Is your company legally certified and operationally equipped to accept, stow, and transport all the specific classes of hazardous waste listed? (See attached �DLA-GUAM � Hazardous Waste List�.) 5. Volume and Throughput Capacity? (Critical): 6. What is the maximum volume (measured in standard Conex/ISO container equivalents) that your company can commit to transporting on this route per week for the DoW, and DoW Contractors for the Hazard Class/UN Number Required? 7. Can your company meet or exceed the military's minimum required throughput of 2 Each � 40-Foot Container�s (or equivalent) without causing operational or regulatory storage backlogs in Guam? 8. If your company can only offer partial or restricted capacity (e.g., limiting transport to 1 container per week/voyage), please provide specific operational, regulatory, or safety constraints dictating this volume limit. Commercial Intent: If your company possesses both the technical capability and the required volume capacity, is your company willing to support the DoW, and DoW Contractors executing the removal of hazardous waste from Guam? Justification for Refusal: If your company is unable or unwilling to accept this cargo, or cannot meet the required weekly volume throughput, please state the specific technical, regulatory, safety, or vessel allocation reasons for your refusal/capacity limitation. This RFI-Market Research does not constitute a solicitation and does not obligate the Government to issue a solicitation, award a contract, or pay for information submitted in response to this notice. The Government will utilize the provided data, as well as any omissions, to assess commercial capability, capacity, availability, procurement strategies, and hazardous waste transportation exceptions. Please submit your written response directly to Bradley Moehlig at Bradley.Moehlig@dla.mil & Mike Mamaty at Michael.Mamaty@dla.mil . Submissions should be delivered electronically via email in Adobe PDF or Microsoft Word format. Please referencing Subject Line: 'Response to RFI � Maritime Transport of Hazardous Waste (Guam to CONUS)'. Timely submission of capabilities, vessel availability, and commercial operating constraints will directly inform DLA's acquisition strategy, small business determinations, and required statutory compliance determinations under federal maritime law.

description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products prepared in accordance with the format in Revolutionary FAR Overhaul FAR Subpart 12.2, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. The solicitation number is 15B50527Q00000008 and is issued as a Request for Quote (RFQ). This Solicitation is for 2nd Qtr FY27 National Menu Solicitation. The solicitation document, incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Revolutionary FAR Overhaul issuance date May 2, 2025. This solicitation is issued as Total small business set-aside. The associated North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 311999 with a small business size standard of 700.00 employees. FOB Destination shall be to: FMC Carswell Food Service Department 1200 Meandering Road, Fort Worth, Texas 76114. Items will be awarded individually. More than one item may be awarded to one offeror/contractor. Award will be given to the offeror whose bid/quote conforms to the requirements and is determined to provide the best value to the Government. The following are the evaluation factors that will be used to evaluate each offeror are price, past performance and conformity to applicable and requested specifications. Past performance and specification conformity are significantly as important as price. Quotes shall be accepted up to 4 decimal places. DELIVERY REQUIREMENTS/INSTRUCTIONS: Product(s) must meet Certified Menu Specifications; must have a legible expiration date that is at least 6 months past date delivered or will not be accepted No dented cans All boxes/cases must be properly labeled (no write on labels or crossed out labels) All deliveries must be palletized unless prior arrangements were agreed to by warehouse staff. All non-frozen, perishable foods must be delivered between 34 degrees F and 40 degrees F. All canned goods must be delivered above 34 degrees F and not frozen. Any product that indicates prior thawing will be refused. All items must strictly follow the BOP Religious Diet Specifications. Food Service contractors have the responsibility of understanding these specifications. Contractors must obtain a copy of the Religious Diet Specifications prior to quoting. All items will be closely inspected. Some items may require thawing and cooking to determine specification compliance. Receipt of delivery may be conditional for a period of three (3) days to allow for adequate examination and testing. Items that fail to meet specifications will be refused. Items which are conditionally received and found noncompliant must be picked up at the vendors� expense within (2) weeks of noncompliance notification. If the product is not picked up within two (2) weeks, it will be disposed of by warehouse staff. Items that fail to meet specifications will be refused. All items must be dated. Deliveries will be accepted from 7:30 a.m. to 2:00 pm CST, Monday through Fridays, No deliveries on weekends or federal holidays. Delivery is on a first - come, first - serve basis. No delivery appointment is required. For any further delivery queries contact our Warehouse Supervisor at 817-782-4268. Unless otherwise stated within the specification of an item description in Section 2 of SF Form 1449, all dates for frozen food items must be delivered frozen and delivered before the best buy date, sell by date, use by date, best if used by date, or freeze by date on the label. Delivery vehicles should not exceed Gross 49000lbs-Tandem Axle 32000 Lbs. to comply with the bridge weight limit along the delivery route to the warehouse. Please mark all deliveries to reflect: Attn Food Service Department. Payments will be made upon complete delivery and acceptance of the product. Awards will be made via purchase order (EFT). Invoices are to be sent electronically to CRW-BusinessOffice-S@bop.gov. Requested delivery period is January 4 - January 29, 2026. Offerors are solely responsible for ensuring that their small business representations and certifications are current and accurately reflected within their SAM.gov entity profile. The Government's obligation under this solicitation is contingent upon the availability of appropriate funds from which payment for contract purposes can be made. title: Construction Services for replacing the wire ropes and designated associated sheave blocks, Franklin, New Hampshire.
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, New England District is issuing this Sources Sought Announcement for Construction Services for the replacing the wire ropes and designated associated sheave blocks for the number 1 service gate of the dam at the Franklin Falls Dam in Franklin NH. This announcement is to determine interest, availability and capability of 8(a), HUBZone, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned, Women-Owned and Small Business concerns for this project. The NAICS code for this procurement is 237990 with a size standard of $22M. The project is planned to be solicited in the Spring of 2027 with construction to begin place in the Spring/Summer of 2027. The estimated construction cost is between $350,000 - $500,000. The project site is the inlet culvert on the lake side of the Franklin Falls Dam in Franklin, NH. Work for this project will likely include, but not be limited to, the following: Replace the existing stainless steel wire ropes that operate the number 1 service gate. Wire ropes must meet the following conditions: Meet US Steel Manufacture Requirements. Shall be 1,085 linear feet of 1� X 6X26 GALV XIP IWRC RRL PLAIN ENDS. The wire rope shall have a minimum breaking strength of 100 tons. The wire rope shall be lubed during the time of manufacture with accepted lubrication. Specification sections 35 01 70.13 and 35 20 16.53 will be included in the solicitation. Wire rope clips and thimbles will be designed by the contractor for this project and must fully conform with ASME B30 standards and proper amount of clips shall be provided for wire rope size and requirements for proper wire rope turnback. Remove and replace the lower sheave block assembly (five total) that is associated with the number 1 service gate. The following will be applicable for these assemblies: Sheave pins and bushings. Site plates, hitch plates, keeper plates Tap bolts, pipe separator and bolts Hitch pins Finishes and paint Contractors shall install the wire ropes and lower sheave blocks according to appropriate industry standards for Load Handling Equipment of this type and configuration. Interested firms should submit a capabilities package to include the following: business classification (i.e. HUBZone, small business, etc.), as well as qualifications and experience in performing the work components stated above. Please include at least two specific examples of the firm�s experience performing the work requirements stated above. The projects must have been performed within the last seven years. Please indicate the team subcontractor(s) (if any), including their prior experience and qualifications, which will be used to support the offeror�s effort, and their experience must also have been performed within the last seven years. Proof of bonding capability is required. Responses are limited to twenty pages. Responses are due by 25 November 2026 at 1:00 PM Eastern. Responses should be emailed to: Distephano Marcellus � Distephano.Marcellus@usace.army.mil Phone Contact: (978) 318-8890 Interested firms shall provide the above documentation in one original form and one copy. The Government will not pay for any material provided in response to this market survey nor return the data provided. This notice is for information purposes only and is not a request to be placed on a solicitation mailing list nor is it a Request for Proposal (RFP) or an announcement of a solicitation. The results of this survey will be considered to be in effect for a period of one year from the date of this notice. title: Lunar Node - 2 Radio System
description: NASA/MSFC has a requirement for the development and delivery of hardware and firmware for the Lunar Node - 2 payload to support a rapid path to integration and flight payload development. Key considerations of this action are focused on the ability to deliver a flight-ready payload within 90 days, which requires maintaining physical, electrical, and software interfaces to the existing design. NASA/MSFC intends to issue a sole source contract to acquire the following items and services from Amergint Technologies Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of CACI, Inc.-Federal under the authority of FAR 6.103-1, 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), "Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements." Amergint is uniquely qualified to complete this work as the designer, developer, implementer, and owner of the SWIFT-SLX platform. Selection of Amergint utilizes their existing hardware and proprietary technology (including its structure, electronics, interfaces, and antenna) for this mission to meet the project's accelerated deadline while also upgrading capability without requiring interface changes that would impact schedule. The procurement includes multiple potential tasks/items as necessary to prepare the payload for a future flight opportunity: (1) A study to provide insight and detailed schedule for development time for addition of two-way coherent ranging into the flight platform. Analyze and assess feasibility for potential paths for upgrades and improvements to the existing SWIFT SLX-X EDU that the Lunar Node - 1 project has on-hand to support potential lunar operations as part of Lunar Node - 2. Utilize existing hardware from the Lunar Node - 1 payload, including its structure, electronics, interfaces, and antenna. To meet the desired deadline while also adding upgraded capability of high value to the program, the payload cannot accommodate any interface changes. This includes onboard firmware, software, electrical, and mechanical interfaces. (2) Re-work on the existing SWIFT-SLX previously delivered to MSFC. This includes disassembly, conformal coating and staking of internal electronics, reassembly and functional checkouts. (3) A current build of the SWIFT-SLX for an Engineering Development Unit (EDU) and flight platform. (4) A new EDU to match current capabilities and flight design. (5) Upgraded firmware to enable additional capability on the LN-1 SWIFT-SLX radio to enable two-way coherent ranging on the platform using S-band frequencies. The Government intends to acquire a commercial product or service using FAR Part 12. Interested organizations may submit their capabilities and qualifications to perform the effort electronically via email to Cynthia Hubbard at cynthia.a.hubbard@nasa.gov and Brent Evans at brent.l.evans@nasa.gov not later than 12:00 P.M. C.D.T. on November 25, 2026. Such capabilities/qualifications will be evaluated solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct this acquisition on a competitive basis. A decision by the Government not to compete this acquisition on a full and open competition basis, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the Government. NASA Clause 1852.215-84, Ombudsman, is applicable. The Center Ombudsman for this acquisition can be found at: https://www.hq.nasa.gov/office/procurement/regs/Procurement-Ombuds- Comp-Advocate-Listing.pdf

title: FMC Carswell 2 QTR FY27 Religious Diet & Milk Menu
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products prepared in accordance with the format in Revolutionary FAR Overhaul FAR Subpart 12.2, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. The solicitation number is 15B50527Q00000006 and is issued as a Request for Quote (RFQ). This Solicitation is for 2nd Qtr. FY27 Religious Diet & Milk Menu. The solicitation document, incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Revolutionary FAR Overhaul issuance date May 2, 2025. This solicitation is issued as Total small business set-aside. The associated North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 311999 with a small business size standard of 700.00 employees. FOB Destination shall be to: FMC Carswell Food Service Department 1200 Meandering Road, Fort Worth, Texas 76114. Items will be awarded individually. More than one item may be awarded to one offeror/contractor. Award will be given to the offeror whose bid/quote conforms to the requirements and is determined to provide the best value to the Government. The following are the evaluation factors that will be used to evaluate each offeror are price, past performance and best value (conformity to applicable and requested specifications). Past performance and specification conformity are significantly as important as price. Quotes shall be accepted up to 4 decimal places. DELIVERY REQUIREMENTS/INSTRUCTIONS: Product(s) must meet Certified Menu Specifications; must have a legible expiration date that is at least 6 months past date delivered or will not be accepted No dented cans All boxes/cases must be properly labeled (no write on labels or crossed out labels) All deliveries must be palletized unless prior arrangements were agreed to by warehouse staff. All non-frozen, perishable foods must be delivered between 34 degrees F and 40 degrees F. All canned goods must be delivered above 34 degrees F and not frozen. Any product that indicates prior thawing will be refused. All items must strictly follow the BOP Religious Diet Specifications. Food Service contractors have the responsibility of understanding these specifications. Contractors must obtain a copy of the Religious Diet Specifications prior to quoting. All items will be closely inspected. Some items may require thawing and cooking to determine specification compliance. Receipt of delivery may be conditional for a period of three (3) days to allow for adequate examination and testing. Items that fail to meet specifications will be refused. Items which are conditionally received and found noncompliant must be picked up at the vendors� expense within (2) weeks of noncompliance notification. If the product is not picked up within two (2) weeks, it will be disposed of by warehouse staff. Items that fail to meet specifications will be refused. All items must be dated. Deliveries will be accepted from 7:30 a.m. to 2:00 pm CST, Monday through Fridays, No deliveries on weekends or federal holidays. Delivery is on a first - come, first - serve basis. No delivery appointment is required. For any further delivery queries contact our Warehouse Supervisor at 817-782-4268. title: NAWCAD HX-21 CH-53K ORGANIZATIONAL LEVEL CONTRACTOR MAINTENANCE SUPPORT (CMS)
description: 1.0 INTRODUCTION a. The Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division (NAWCAD), Naval Test Wing Atlantic (NTWL), Air Test and Evaluation Squadron TWO ONE (HX-21), Patuxent River, MD, has a follow-on requirement for Contractor Maintenance Support (CMS) Services to perform Organizational Level (O-Level) maintenance support services on assigned CH-53K test aircraft. This Market Research tool is being used to identify potential and eligible firms, of all sizes, prior to determining the method of acquisition and issuance of a solicitation. The results of the Sources Sought will be utilized to determine if any Small Business Set[1]Aside opportunities exist. Additionally, this Sources Sought is being used to gather constructive information from industry to improve the Request for Proposal (RFP). This is for the NAWCAD HX-21 CH-53K O-LEVEL CMS. This is a follow-on requirement. The current contract information can be found in Section 3.0, paragraph b below. There have been significant changes to the scope as follows: estimated on-site personnel increasing from 62 FTEs to 75 FTEs. This is not subject to bundling or consolidation. b. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. 3.0 ANTICIPATED CONTRACT TYPE AND CONTRACT/PROGRAM BACKGROUND a. Anticipated Contract Type: C-Type Contract with Firm Fixed Price (FFP) CLINs for Labor and Cost Reimbursable CLINs for associated Other Direct Costs (ODCs). The Government is anticipating an additional Cost Reimbursable Performance Incentive CLIN. The anticipated Period of Performance includes one base period of 12 months with four one[1]year option periods for a total potential performance period of 5 years. b. The incumbent contract information is as follows: Incumbent Contractor: Adams Communication & Engineering Technology, Inc. Program Background: HX-21 has a follow-on requirement for CMS Services to perform O-Level (to include limited Intermediate Level (I-Level) and Depot Level (D[1]Level)) maintenance support services and other explicit test support tasks required to maintain assigned CH-53K aircraft to the proper standards required to meet the requirements of the HX-21 test schedule. The test schedule includes both flight and ground test events to meet the PMA-261 and other requirement owner program performance needs. The limited I-Level and D-Level work is contingent, provided skilled artisans and required tools are available and authorization is received from the cognizant authority. Services include aircraft maintenance and logistics support on aircraft, aircraft systems, and Support Equipment (SE) for which HX-21 has cognizant responsibility. Additional services include maintenance of prototype aircraft components, configuration and installation of internal/external ballast, and Helicopter Support Team (HST) duties, i.e. external sling load operations. The majority of work performance will be accomplished at Patuxent River, Maryland. Additional temporary work sites in direct support of projects are executed as detachments and include (but are not limited to) United States Naval Vessels, Department of War Installations, and Commercial Facilities which also encompass unscheduled emergent type maintenance support. title: Trenching, Conduit and Ground-well Installation
description: Description The United Stated Embassy in Kingston is requesting proposals for Trenching, Conduit And Ground-Well Installation in various locations on the Embassy compound. The contractor will provide all labor, equipment, supervision, material specific to the back filling and compaction and management needed to complete the job Infrastructure Support System - Handhole / Underground Conduit System Trenching Nine locations have been identified requiring trench work. Thirteen locations have been identified requiring trench work. Before excavation, the Contractor shall locate and verify all existing utilities in the proposed trench alignment. If excavation interferes with existing drains, piping, or structures, the Contractor shall immediately notify, in writing, the COR and provide temporary protection for these systems before proceeding. Trenching from Handholes The Contractor shall make wall penetrations into existing manholes/handholes as required for the number and size of conduits entering and exiting each structure, in accordance with the drawings. Conduit Existing conduit shall remain in place unless the drawings specifically direct removal or modification. Under grass, soil, the Contractor shall install Schedule 80 PVC conduit with a minimum cover of 24 inches (610 mm) from finished grade to top of conduit, or as indicated on the drawings, whichever is greater. All underground 90 degree bends with a 12inch (305 mm) radius shall use prefabricated sweeping bends. Above grade, all underground PVC conduit shall transition to rigid galvanized steel (RGS) using PVC to RGS couplers. The Contractor shall install pull lines in all new conduit runs. Soil and Backfill Materials Soil Materials The Contractor shall provide all labor and materials for soil and backfill, where required. Select Backfill: ASTM D 2487 soil classification groups SW, SP, and SM, or combinations thereof; free of rock or gravel larger than 3 inches (75 mm), debris, waste, frozen materials, vegetation, and other deleterious matter. Asphalt/Concrete Base Course: Naturally or artificially graded mixture of natural or crushed gravel, crushed stone, and natural or crushed sand; ASTM D 2940; with at least 95% passing a 11/2inch (40 mm) sieve and not more than 8% passing a 1/4inch (6.4 mm) sieve. Base Gravel: Naturally or artificially graded mixture of natural or crushed gravel, crushed stone, and natural or crushed sand; ASTM D 2940; 100% passing a 1inch (25 mm) sieve and not more than 8% passing a 1/4inch (6.4 mm) sieve. Sand Cushion: ASTM C 33 fine aggregate, natural or manufactured sand. Placement and Compaction Place backfill and fill in layers not exceeding: 8 inches (203 mm) loose thickness for heavy compaction equipment; 4 inches (102 mm) loose thickness when compacted by hand-operated tampers. Place backfill and fill evenly to the required elevations, uniformly along their full length. Compact soil materials to not less than the following percentages of maximum dry unit weight per ASTM D 1557: Under lawns or unpaved areas: scarify and re-compact top 6 inches (152 mm) below subgrade and compact each layer to 85%. Utility trenches: compact each layer of initial and final backfill to 85%. The Chesapeake and Delaware or Canal connects the Delaware River to the Chesapeake Bay and Port of Baltimore. The canal is maintained from a field office located in Chesapeake City Maryland. This office consists of multiple buildings and shops that are essential to the continued operation of the canal. Several of these building have reached the end of their lifecycle and need to be replaced. This project will include the demolition and consolidation of the mechanics shop, bridge shop and storage buildings. A new building will be constructed to sever as a replacement of the buildings that are being removed. The building will be located along the east side of the project site. The building dimensions will be 60 feet x 150 feet with a clear ceiling height of 20 feet. The building will have a gable roof with the ridge running parallel to the length of the building. A pre- engineered metal building with tapered columns will be used. The columns will be enclosed with steel stud framing and gypsum board in the office areas. Vehicle and workshop areas will have propane fired heating. Office areas will be provided with air conditioning. The electrical service will be upgraded if necessary to provide power to the new building. The building will be connected into backup power from the existing diesel generator. Work will consist of the following activities: A.) The project scope includes all work required to design and construct a 9,000 square foot maintenance building in accordance with the Request for Proposal documents including the demolition of the four existing buildings and propane storage tank currently located at the site. Utilities serving each of the buildings being demolished must be demolished to the extents defined in section 02 41 00 Demolition. Requirements stated in this contract are minimums. Innovative, creative, and life cycle cost effective solutions, which meet or exceed these requirements are encouraged. Further, the Offeror is encouraged to seek solutions that will expedite construction (panelization, pre-engineered, etc.) and shorten the schedule. The intent of the Government is to emphasize the placement of funds into functional/operational requirements. Materials and methods must reflect this by choosing the most economical type of construction allowed by code for this occupancy/project. B.) The maintenance building must be provided with Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC), electrical, communications, fire protection, life safety, plumbing systems, waste oil storage, and compressed air systems. C.) A 3,000 square foot storage shed must be designed and constructed at the location identified on the site plan. The shed design must include power and lighting. D.) The scope of work also includes civil site work consisting of site paving, installation of stormwater drainage, connection into the domestic water utility, sanitary sewer utility connection for the new maintenance building, connection of existing sanitary sewer lines into the towns sanitary sewer utility, a vehicle wash area and fire hydrants. Site work is shown in Appendix A. Site electrical work must be completed to provide the maintenance building and storage shed with power fed from the existing switch gear shed. Site telecommunications work must be completed to provide the maintenance building with connection into the existing telecommunications utilities. E.) A propane storage tank must be provided onsite and be connected to the new maintenance building and the existing propane fired generator. The estimated period of performance will be 730 calendar days. The estimated magnitude of this project is between $5,000,000 and $15,000,000. The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code is 236220 Commercial and Institutional Building Construction, with an SBA Size standard of $45.0M.

title: Veterans Affairs St. Louis Health Care System (VASTLHCS) John Cochran (JC) Hospital in St. Louis, Missouri
description: ****Amend 0006 posted 20261023: Provide additional updates based on bidder inquiries****Amend 0005 posted 20261021: Provide additional updates based on bidder inquiries****Amend 0004 posted 20261002: Provide additional updates based on bidder inquiries****Amend 0003 posted 20260925: Provide updates based on bidder inquiries****Amend 0002 posted 20260902: Provide specifics for the site visit****Amend 0001 posted 20260817: Provide correct Plans Room Key****VA Hospital Solicitation Notice W912DQ26RA060. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Kansas City District is issuing a solicitation for an Integrated Design and Construction (IDaC) services delivery method contract for the construction of a new bed tower, clinical expansion, parking garage in support of the Veterans Affairs St. Louis Health Care System (VASTLHCS) John Cochran (JC) Hospital in St. Louis, Missouri. Offerors shall submit an offer subject to Project Labor Agreement (PLA) requirements in accordance with RFO 22.5, Project Labor Agreements for Federal Construction Projects. Any PLA reached pursuant to the PLA requirements in the solicitation does not change the terms of the contract or provide for any price adjustment by the Government. Funds are fully available for this requirement. The project will be solicited as full and open (unrestricted). The requirements under this construction project include right sizing the VAs medical center by demolishing several deficient and underutilized buildings and then constructing multiple new modern and seismically compliant structures and facilities on the same, expanded site. The newly constructed facilities are incorporated into a master plan for future expansion and demolition of additional primary facilities. The new primary facilities will be acquired using the Integrated Design and Construction (IDaC) delivery method which includes a Pre-Construction Services Phase. The Government will evaluate the performance capability of offerors in accordance with the criteria described in the solicitation resulting in a single award under the best value continuum using the trade-off process in accordance with RFO 15.103-1 to the responsible offeror whose proposal the source selection authority determines conforms to the solicitation, is fair and reasonable, and offers the best overall value to the government, considering non-priced factors described in the solicitation and price. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 236220, (Commercial and Institutional Building Construction), with a small business size standard of $45 million in average annual receipts. The estimated construction magnitude is over $1,000,000,000. The estimated performance period for the pre-construction services phase is 820 calendar days from Notice to Proceed (NTP).Interested offerors must have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM). If the offeror is a Joint Venture (JV), the JV entity must have valid SAM registration in the SAM database representing the JV as one business/firm/entity. A Proposal Guarantee will be required with your proposal in the amount of 20% of the Offerors proposed price or $3,000,000, whichever is less. Payment and Performance Bonds will be required for the full amount (100%) of the awarded contract before the Notice to Proceed can be issued. Point of Contact: The point of contact for all questions/inquiries is Michael France at michael.g.france@usace.army.mil and David Walsh (Contracting Officer) at david.j.walsh@usace.army.mil.

title: USACE - SWG Environmental Services for Evaluation of Dredged Material
description: SOURCES SOUGHT SYNOPSIS The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Galveston District, has a requirement for environmental services supporting evaluation of dredged material and related services. THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. THIS ANNOUNCEMENT SEEKS INFORMATION FROM INDUSTRY THAT WILL BE USED FOR PRELIMINARY PLANNING PURPOSES. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS, REQUEST FOR QUOTATIONS, OR INVITATION FOR BIDS. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A PROCUREMENT COMMITMENT BY THE U.S. ARMY CORPS OF ENGINEERS, IMPLIED OR OTHERWISE. NO CONTRACT WILL BE AWARDED FROM THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE. Responses are strictly voluntary. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this Sources Sought Notice or any follow-up information requests. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the Government�s evaluation. The Government is considering a competitive, single-award, indefinite-delivery, indefinite-quantity (IDIQ) contract with firm-fixed-price task orders. The contemplated ordering period is one 12-month base period and four 12-month option periods. The anticipated maximum contract capacity is up to $10,000,000 over the total ordering period. The final acquisition strategy, including the number of awards, contract type, contract capacity, ordering period, NAICS code, and socioeconomic set-aside decision, will be based on the results of market research and acquisition planning. BASED ON THE RESPONSES TO THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE/MARKET RESEARCH, THIS REQUIREMENT MAY BE SET ASIDE FOR SMALL BUSINESS CONCERNS, IN WHOLE OR IN PART, OR PROCURED THROUGH FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION. ALL SMALL BUSINESS SET-ASIDE CATEGORIES WILL BE CONSIDERED. NO SITE VISIT, PRE-PROPOSAL CONFERENCE, OR INDUSTRY DAY WILL BE HELD. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT The anticipated requirement is for environmental services supporting evaluation of dredged material for placement suitability and assessment of potential effects in terrestrial, marine, estuarine, and freshwater environments. Services will be provided for customers of USACE Galveston District and will be performed principally in Texas and Louisiana. Individual task orders may require work at Government sites, project locations, vessels, laboratories, or contractor facilities. The contractor shall furnish all personnel, management, facilities, equipment, materials, supplies, travel, and services necessary to perform task-order requirements. Services may include, but are not limited to: Collection of water, sediment, soil, elutriate, benthos, nekton, and tissue samples; Physical, chemical, biological, contaminant, grain-size, toxicity, bioassay, and bioaccumulation testing and analysis; Preparation of Sampling and Analysis Plans, Quality Assurance Project Plans, field documentation, laboratory data packages, and technical reports; Preparation of dredged-material evaluation reports supporting Marine Protection, Research, and Sanctuaries Act Section 103 evaluations and Clean Water Act Section 404 evaluations; Environmental modeling, data interpretation, and beneficial-use evaluations; Environmental compliance support, monitoring, surveys, Geographic Information System data, and related special studies; and Other services within the general scope of environmental services for dredged-material evaluation, as specified in individual task orders. A draft Statement of Work/Performance Work Statement is attached for review and comment. State whether the firm has performed similar services as a prime contractor, joint-venture partner, teaming partner, or subcontractor. If yes, provide information for up to three recent projects, including: Customer; Project title and location; Contract or project number, if applicable; Period of performance; Contract value and the respondent�s share of the work; Whether the respondent was the prime contractor, joint-venture partner, teaming partner, or subcontractor; and A brief description of the services performed. Capability and Capacity. Describe the firm�s capability to perform the anticipated work, including field sampling, laboratory testing, bioassays, data management, environmental modeling, preparation of Section 103 and Section 404 evaluation reports, technical-report preparation, quality control, and management of multiple concurrent task orders. Identify any anticipated subcontractors, teaming partners, or laboratories and the work they would perform. Small-Business Capability. If the respondent is a small business, identify the major services the firm anticipates self-performing and the major services anticipated to be performed by subcontractors or teaming partners. Acquisition Feedback. State: Whether the firm is interested in submitting a proposal if a solicitation is issued; Whether the firm has the capability and capacity to support a contract with an anticipated maximum capacity of up to $10,000,000 over five years; Whether a single-award IDIQ contract is an appropriate vehicle for this requirement; and Any concerns or recommended revisions regarding the attached draft SOW, including unclear requirements, restrictive requirements, specialized testing or equipment needs, laboratory capacity, or other factors that may affect competition or performance. Questions concerning this Sources Sought Notice must be submitted by email to SFC Seth Teasdale at seth.k.teasdale@usace.army.mil no later than 2:00 p.m. Central Time, 23 November 2026. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted. The Government may use information received to refine the requirement and acquisition strategy. Information marked proprietary will be handled in accordance with applicable Government procedures.

title: GSA Fleet Lease Vehicle Marshalling Services - Yuma, AZ
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION: GSA Fleet Lease Vehicle Marshalling Services 1.0 Description The General Services Administration (GSA) Office of Fleet Management (GSA Fleet) has a requirement to acquire contractor support for vehicle auction and marshalling services or marshalling only services for Government vehicles. Services are required on or about January 1, 2027 � December 31, 2030 in Yuma, AZ. Interested parties must be located within 50 miles of the Yuma, AZ area. The vendor must be the owner or legal lessee of the facility. Auction and marshalling site tasks include, but are not limited to: Advise the government on optimal disposition strategy for individual exchange/sale-eligible vehicles worldwide to maximize public participation and net proceeds, to include strategies for specialty (law enforcement, buses, ambulances, medium & heavy trucks, etc.) as well as Zero Emission Vehicles to include battery electric vehicles, plug-in hybrid vehicles and/or fuel cell vehicles. Perform full vehicle inspections and ensure complete condition reporting, imagery capture (including high-definition photo and video, 360� views, etc.), and accurate description writing. Provide recommendations on vehicle repairs and pricing, given vehicle condition, market environment, among any other factors, to ensure the greatest return on investment. Create and execute marketing plans/campaigns to catalog vehicles and announce vehicle sales to the public as required by law, and to advertise to/connect with the broadest possible market audience. Perform electronic inventory management for vehicles and vehicle-related assets (e.g., license plates, removed equipment, telematics devices). Support the creation and management of all required vehicle disposition documentation/records. Conduct activities related to bidder/buyer management, including registration, validation/eligibility checks, etc. Provide end-to-end customer service and support to bidders/buyers throughout the sales process to ensure a seamless, transparent, and customer-centric buying experience. Facilitate and perform payment collection process. Encourage maximum participation by offering a range of non-government affiliated services (retail financing, aftermarket warranties, vehicle enhancement etc.). Store, service and remarket of electric vehicles to include any necessary charging infrastructure. Transport vehicles to and from vendor locations. Prepare vehicles for public inspection and final sales/disposition, including services such as reconditioning, maintenance and repair, as well as equipment removal/disposal, and license plate & government credit card disposal and tracking. Offer industry-aligned services for customers to perform vehicle test drives. Provide state-of-the-art technology that will improve customer experience including enhanced condition reporting, 360� views, video, high-definition photography, etc. Conduct a full and open competitive sales process, including public inspection periods for all vehicles, and any related sale services for exchange/sale property. Ensure and facilitate the security, storage, and release of vehicles from time of receipt until final removal. Manage the logistics of vehicle transportation to bring vehicles to sale. Prepare vehicles for sale, to include vehicle equipment removal/disposal, reconditioning, and repairs. Work with local government entities to facilitate any inspections, documentation, and any other actions required to complete transactions in local markets. Perform electronic inventory management, vehicle inspection, complete condition reporting for vehicles. Offer recommendations on vehicle repairs and pricing, given vehicle condition, local market environment, among any other factors, to ensure the greatest return on investment. Provide customer service to buyers in global markets. Create and execute marketing campaigns for local markets. Offer an internet sales platform with the potential to reach a global audience. Collect proceeds from vehicle sales and if necessary, convert to U.S. dollars. Marshalling only site tasks include, but are not limited to: Transport or resource/transportation of vehicles to and from vendor location (e.g., customer location, OEM dealership, offsite repair facility). Inspect vehicles upon delivery for various factors including but not limited to any damage to the vehicle, all components of the vehicle are accounted for (e.g., keys, floor mats, etc.), and missing equipment. Perform telematics device installation and/or activation on all new vehicles prior to releasing the vehicle to the customer. Validate new vehicles and options to vehicle order information provided by GSA. Perform pre-delivery inspections (PDI) in accordance with the manufacturer�s standards. Prepare new vehicles for customer receipt. Provide driver education for customers including vehicle operation, unique features, infotainment settings, etc. Offer specialized expertise and support on Electric Vehicle management, operation and charging infrastructure. Charge battery-powered vehicles. Maintain all vehicle fuel and charge levels as prescribed in the Statement of Work by GSA. Perform custodial and sales preparation services to facilitate auction house sales of GSA exchange lease vehicles. Process and manage all required vehicle shipment and delivery documentation. Manage scheduled vehicle appointments and ensure accurate vehicle exchanges. Perform all necessary tasks associated with confirming vehicle assignment and termination to and from the customer as prescribed by GSA. Provide end-to-end customer service and support to GSA Fleet and customer agencies throughout the marshalling process to ensure a seamless and transparent delivery and exchange process. Fulfill proper disposal of old/expired plates both front and back as prescribed by GSA. Perform electronic inventory management for vehicles. Ensure and facilitate the security, storage and inventory control of vehicles, license plates, credit cards and other assets from time of receipt until final removal. Scale charging capabilities to meet the needs of increasing electric vehicle adoption. 2.0 Background GSA Fleet provides a full-service fleet management program providing transportation solutions to partner agencies worldwide across the U.S. Federal government. It maintains a diverse fleet of over 250,000 vehicles, including light, medium, and heavy-duty vehicles, to include sedans, SUVs, vans, trucks, buses, ambulances, and law enforcement vehicles. Vehicles range from gasoline and diesel fueled vehicles to alternative fuel vehicles (AFVs), such as electric vehicles (EVs) to low-speed electric vehicles (LSEV�s) and non-powered vehicles and trailers. Nationally, GSA Fleet orders and receives on average 30,000+ vehicles from suppliers annually. As GSA Fleet is responsible for the disposition of its vehicles, it then remarkets and sells the used vehicles across the United States and its territories, Japan, and Europe. Its vehicles are sold under the exchange/sale authority of 41 CFR 102-39. This authority aims to expedite the disposal process and maximize proceeds in the most cost-effective manner to the U.S. taxpayer. To achieve this objective, GSA Fleet currently sells its used vehicles via live and online auctions worldwide, leveraging its contracts with commercial vendors to carry out all auction-related services. These auctions must adhere to all legal and regulatory requirements. They must also be open to the general public and provide an equal opportunity for individuals, businesses, government entities, and other organizations to take part in a zero-fee, fully open, and competitive sales process. To facilitate this process, GSA Fleet employs its vehicle remarketing specialists, who are warranted sales contracting officers and experts in the sales of its vehicles, to work with its vendors to approve repairs, pricing, as well as carry out and approve each sale to maximize net proceeds.
