title: Enterprise Inbound Email Retention and Forensic Analysis Solution
description: Enterprise Inbound Email Retention and Forensic Analysis Solution Sources Sought Notice / Request for Information (RFI) This is a Sources Sought Notice (SSN) for market research purposes only. This notice is issued solely for information and acquisition planning purposes and does not constitute a Request for Quotation (RFQ), Request for Proposal (RFP), or a commitment to issue a solicitation in the future. The Internal Revenue Service (IRS) does not obligate itself to contract for any supply or service as a result of this notice. The Government is not currently seeking quotations or proposals and will not accept unsolicited quotations. The purpose of this notice is to identify potential vendors and commercially available solutions capable of meeting the IRS's enterprise email retention, search, and forensic analysis requirements. 1. BACKGROUND The Department of the Treasury, Internal Revenue Service (IRS), is seeking information on existing Commercial-Off-the-Shelf (COTS) solutions capable of providing enterprise-wide inbound email visibility, retention, centralized search, and forensic analysis capabilities for both legitimate (clean) and malicious emails. The IRS currently utilizes Cisco IronPort email security infrastructure and an existing Blind Carbon Copy (BCC) method to receive and retain copies of inbound email messages. The IRS is seeking a solution that can integrate with this existing infrastructure and preserve complete, unaltered copies of inbound emails, including message headers, content, metadata, and attachments. The IRS requires an enterprise-level solution that operates independently of individual Microsoft Outlook clients and does not rely on Outlook add-ons, plug-ins, or client-side software for enterprise email collection, retention, search, and forensic analysis. The IRS is interested in commercially available on-premises, virtual, cloud-based, or hybrid solutions. The Government is also interested in alternative technical approaches that can provide equivalent capabilities while meeting applicable federal security and operational requirements. The IRS does not have a predefined solution or architecture and welcomes information on commercially available products capable of meeting its operational needs. The results of this market research will assist the Government in identifying potential sources, assessing available commercial capabilities, and determining an appropriate acquisition strategy. The IRS anticipates a target implementation date of June 2027. Interested vendors should identify their estimated delivery and implementation timelines. 2. TECHNICAL CAPABILITIES Interested vendors are requested to describe their ability to meet the following anticipated technical and operational capabilities. Vendors should identify any capabilities that cannot be met or would require additional configuration, integration, or development. The Government welcomes information on alternative approaches that achieve equivalent operational outcomes. A. Cisco IronPort Integration and Email Collection Support integration with Cisco IronPort to receive and retain complete, unaltered copies of inbound email messages, including legitimate (clean) and malicious emails, through the existing BCC method or an alternative collection method that provides equivalent functionality. Preserve original message headers, content, metadata, and attachments for forensic investigations. Provide enterprise-wide email collection independent of Microsoft Outlook add-ons, plug-ins, or client-side applications. Identify any additional infrastructure, software, or configuration required for integration. B. Enterprise Email Volume and Retention The solution should be capable of supporting the following estimated email volumes: Up to approximately 1 million inbound emails per day. Peak email volume of approximately 150,000 emails per hour. Approximately 22 TB of inbound email data per month. Configurable retention periods ranging from 30 to 180 days for both legitimate and malicious emails. Vendors should describe the scalability, storage architecture, and performance capabilities of their proposed solutions. C. Email Search and Forensic Analysis Provide centralized search and investigation capabilities for both legitimate and malicious inbound email messages. Allow authorized analysts to search, retrieve, and review complete email messages, including headers, metadata, and attachments. Describe the solution's capabilities for identifying and classifying potentially malicious email messages, including any integration with existing email security tools. Describe available quarantine or equivalent isolation capabilities, whether provided directly by the solution or through integration with existing security infrastructure. Allow authorized analysts to view and download attachments for forensic investigations. Maintain message integrity throughout the retention and investigation process. D. Third-Party Integration Support integration with Splunk for forwarding system logs, events, and email metadata. Support integration with Splunk SOAR for investigation and response automation. Provide APIs or equivalent interfaces for integration with additional security tools and automated workflows. E. Administration and System Management Provide secure command-line interface (CLI) access or equivalent administrative capabilities. Support high availability, redundancy, and automatic failover. Provide centralized system configuration, administration, and monitoring. For physical on-premises appliances, support IPMI or equivalent out-of-band hardware management. F. Security and Federal Compliance The solution must be capable of supporting applicable federal cybersecurity and audit requirements, including: IPv6 compatibility. Applicable FIPS 140-2 or FIPS 140-3 validated cryptographic modules. Encryption of data at rest and in transit. Role-based access control (RBAC). Audit logging and monitoring. Configurable security warning banners. Secure input validation. Secure remote configuration backups. Active Directory integration, including LDAP and SAML-based authentication, as applicable. For cloud-based solutions, vendors shall identify their FedRAMP authorization status, authorization level, and any limitations or additional requirements associated with federal deployment. Vendors shall also identify the country of product development, hosting locations, data storage locations, and any applicable federal security or supply-chain considerations. G. Technical Support and Maintenance Provide information regarding 24x7 technical support availability. Identify whether technical support can be provided by U.S.-citizen personnel. Describe regular software updates, security patches, and vulnerability remediation procedures. Identify available maintenance agreements, support response times, and escalation procedures. 3. SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS a) Point of Contact The point of contact for this notice is: Contracting Officer: Jessica Camunez Email: Jessica.r.camunez@irs.gov Responses shall be submitted electronically no later than November 25, 2026, at 3:00 PM, Eastern Time. Vendors shall reference "Enterprise Inbound Email Retention and Forensic Analysis Solution" in the subject line of their response. The Government is not requesting formal quotations, proposals, or general marketing materials. b) Requested Vendor Information The Government requests that interested parties submit the following information: 1. Company name, Unique Entity ID (UEI), business address, point of contact, telephone number, and email address. 2. Business size and socioeconomic status (e.g., large business, small business, small disadvantaged business, HUBZone, woman-owned small business, service-disabled veteran-owned small business). 3. title: GSA Fleet Lease Vehicle Marshalling Services - Yuma, AZ
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION: GSA Fleet Lease Vehicle Marshalling Services 1.0 Description The General Services Administration (GSA) Office of Fleet Management (GSA Fleet) has a requirement to acquire contractor support for vehicle auction and marshalling services or marshalling only services for Government vehicles. Services are required on or about January 1, 2027 � December 31, 2030 in Yuma, AZ. Interested parties must be located within 50 miles of the Yuma, AZ area. The vendor must be the owner or legal lessee of the facility. Auction and marshalling site tasks include, but are not limited to: Advise the government on optimal disposition strategy for individual exchange/sale-eligible vehicles worldwide to maximize public participation and net proceeds, to include strategies for specialty (law enforcement, buses, ambulances, medium & heavy trucks, etc.) as well as Zero Emission Vehicles to include battery electric vehicles, plug-in hybrid vehicles and/or fuel cell vehicles. Perform full vehicle inspections and ensure complete condition reporting, imagery capture (including high-definition photo and video, 360� views, etc.), and accurate description writing. Provide recommendations on vehicle repairs and pricing, given vehicle condition, market environment, among any other factors, to ensure the greatest return on investment. Create and execute marketing plans/campaigns to catalog vehicles and announce vehicle sales to the public as required by law, and to advertise to/connect with the broadest possible market audience. Perform electronic inventory management for vehicles and vehicle-related assets (e.g., license plates, removed equipment, telematics devices). Support the creation and management of all required vehicle disposition documentation/records. Conduct activities related to bidder/buyer management, including registration, validation/eligibility checks, etc. Provide end-to-end customer service and support to bidders/buyers throughout the sales process to ensure a seamless, transparent, and customer-centric buying experience. Facilitate and perform payment collection process. Encourage maximum participation by offering a range of non-government affiliated services (retail financing, aftermarket warranties, vehicle enhancement etc.). Store, service and remarket of electric vehicles to include any necessary charging infrastructure. Transport vehicles to and from vendor locations. Prepare vehicles for public inspection and final sales/disposition, including services such as reconditioning, maintenance and repair, as well as equipment removal/disposal, and license plate & government credit card disposal and tracking. Offer industry-aligned services for customers to perform vehicle test drives. Provide state-of-the-art technology that will improve customer experience including enhanced condition reporting, 360� views, video, high-definition photography, etc. Conduct a full and open competitive sales process, including public inspection periods for all vehicles, and any related sale services for exchange/sale property. Ensure and facilitate the security, storage, and release of vehicles from time of receipt until final removal. Manage the logistics of vehicle transportation to bring vehicles to sale. Prepare vehicles for sale, to include vehicle equipment removal/disposal, reconditioning, and repairs. Work with local government entities to facilitate any inspections, documentation, and any other actions required to complete transactions in local markets. Perform electronic inventory management, vehicle inspection, complete condition reporting for vehicles. Offer recommendations on vehicle repairs and pricing, given vehicle condition, local market environment, among any other factors, to ensure the greatest return on investment. Provide customer service to buyers in global markets. Create and execute marketing campaigns for local markets. Offer an internet sales platform with the potential to reach a global audience. Collect proceeds from vehicle sales and if necessary, convert to U.S. dollars. Marshalling only site tasks include, but are not limited to: Transport or resource/transportation of vehicles to and from vendor location (e.g., customer location, OEM dealership, offsite repair facility). Inspect vehicles upon delivery for various factors including but not limited to any damage to the vehicle, all components of the vehicle are accounted for (e.g., keys, floor mats, etc.), and missing equipment. Perform telematics device installation and/or activation on all new vehicles prior to releasing the vehicle to the customer. Validate new vehicles and options to vehicle order information provided by GSA. Perform pre-delivery inspections (PDI) in accordance with the manufacturer�s standards. Prepare new vehicles for customer receipt. Provide driver education for customers including vehicle operation, unique features, infotainment settings, etc. Offer specialized expertise and support on Electric Vehicle management, operation and charging infrastructure. Charge battery-powered vehicles. Maintain all vehicle fuel and charge levels as prescribed in the Statement of Work by GSA. Perform custodial and sales preparation services to facilitate auction house sales of GSA exchange lease vehicles. Process and manage all required vehicle shipment and delivery documentation. Manage scheduled vehicle appointments and ensure accurate vehicle exchanges. Perform all necessary tasks associated with confirming vehicle assignment and termination to and from the customer as prescribed by GSA. Provide end-to-end customer service and support to GSA Fleet and customer agencies throughout the marshalling process to ensure a seamless and transparent delivery and exchange process. Fulfill proper disposal of old/expired plates both front and back as prescribed by GSA. Perform electronic inventory management for vehicles. Ensure and facilitate the security, storage and inventory control of vehicles, license plates, credit cards and other assets from time of receipt until final removal. Scale charging capabilities to meet the needs of increasing electric vehicle adoption. 2.0 Background GSA Fleet provides a full-service fleet management program providing transportation solutions to partner agencies worldwide across the U.S. Federal government. It maintains a diverse fleet of over 250,000 vehicles, including light, medium, and heavy-duty vehicles, to include sedans, SUVs, vans, trucks, buses, ambulances, and law enforcement vehicles. Vehicles range from gasoline and diesel fueled vehicles to alternative fuel vehicles (AFVs), such as electric vehicles (EVs) to low-speed electric vehicles (LSEV�s) and non-powered vehicles and trailers. Nationally, GSA Fleet orders and receives on average 30,000+ vehicles from suppliers annually. As GSA Fleet is responsible for the disposition of its vehicles, it then remarkets and sells the used vehicles across the United States and its territories, Japan, and Europe. Its vehicles are sold under the exchange/sale authority of 41 CFR 102-39. This authority aims to expedite the disposal process and maximize proceeds in the most cost-effective manner to the U.S. taxpayer. To achieve this objective, GSA Fleet currently sells its used vehicles via live and online auctions worldwide, leveraging its contracts with commercial vendors to carry out all auction-related services. These auctions must adhere to all legal and regulatory requirements. They must also be open to the general public and provide an equal opportunity for individuals, businesses, government entities, and other organizations to take part in a zero-fee, fully open, and competitive sales process. To facilitate this process, GSA Fleet employs its vehicle remarketing specialists, who are warranted sales contracting officers and experts in the sales of its vehicles, to work with its vendors to approve repairs, pricing, as well as carry out and approve each sale to maximize net proceeds. The Government also reserves the right to cancel this solicitation, either before or after the closing date. 1. Evaluation Criteria and Basis for Award: The Government intends to award one firm-fixed-price purchase order to the responsible quoter whose quotation is determined to be technically acceptable and offers the lowest evaluated total price. Award will be made on a lowest-price technically acceptable (LPTA) basis. Technical acceptability and price are evaluated on a pass/fail basis; no tradeoff will be made between technical merit and price. Technical Acceptability A quotation will be determined technically acceptable when it demonstrates compliance with all material solicitation requirements, including the Statement of Work (SOW), CLIN/Pricing Schedule, and Project Finishes List/Cutsheets. At a minimum, the quoter shall submit: A completed pricing schedule with unit and extended prices for all CLINs; A completed Required Information Sheet; The proposed manufacturer and part number for each sign type; Product literature and cutsheets sufficient to demonstrate compliance with the required sign dimensions, materials, finishes, colors, tactile characters, Braille, insert features, mounting method, and other requirements identified in the SOW and Project Finishes List; For any proposed �or equal� product, documentation demonstrating that the product meets or exceeds all stated salient characteristics and technical requirements; A statement confirming that quoted prices include all supervision, labor, materials, equipment, field verification, fabrication, delivery, removal and disposal of existing signs, patching, painting, mounting hardware, installation, cleanup, warranty, and all other work required by the solicitation; A proposed completion date not later than 120 calendar days after contract award; and A warranty statement consistent with the solicitation requirements. Quotations that take exception to material solicitation requirements, fail to provide required information, or do not demonstrate compliance with the technical requirements may be determined technically unacceptable. Price Evaluation The Government will evaluate the total price by adding the extended prices for all CLINs. Quotations shall include pricing for every CLIN. title: Pilot Training Transformation Device Support Services IV (PTT DSS IV)
description: The purpose of this requirement is to maintain and support PTT device solutions based on state- of-the-art commercial simulation environments, hardware solutions for the cockpit simulation environment, and ancillary software elements.The Contractor shall provide all services and equipment necessary to install, maintain, and support new and existing PTT devices. Devices currently fit into the following classifications: common Immersive Training Device (cITD), enhanced Immersive Training Devices (eITD), and Helicopter Immersive Training Device (HITD). Any new classifications will need to be defined and evaluated prior to inclusion in this scope. The Contractor shall support 142 ITDs and up to 17 Instructor Operating Stations (IOS) at the following locations: Joint Base San Antonio (JBSA) Randolph, TX; Columbus Air Force Base (AFB), MS; Laughlin AFB, TX; Vance AFB, OK, Sheppard AFB, TX; and Fort Rucker, AL. The Government has the right to modify the quantity of devices/locations pending contract modification and funding. The Contractor shall maintain a common software interface to integrate current and future PTT software and hardware components as required by program goals, hardware solutions for the cockpit simulation environment, and on-premises network and data architecture hardware and support, as appropriate for deployed training systems.

Background: The National Institute on Minority Health and Health Disparities (NIMHD) conducts and supports research and training programs to advance knowledge and understanding of health disparities, identify mechanisms to improve minority health and reduce health disparities, and develop effective interventions in community and clinical settings. NIMHD is the lead organization at the National Institutes of Health (NIH) for planning, reviewing, coordinating, and evaluating minority health and health disparities research activities. NIMHD also promotes workforce development, supports research capacity at less-resourced institutions that train students in research careers, serves populations experiencing health disparities, supports participation in clinical research, and promotes information dissemination through regular communications, public education outreach, and scientific presentations. The President�s Executive Order (EO) 14212 Establishing the President�s Make America Healthy Again Commission aims to improve the health of Americans. As described in the EO, escalating burden of chronic diseases poses significant challenges in the United States. These conditions contribute to rising health costs, reduced workforce productivity, and stagnant life expectancies across the country, both in adults and children. NIH defines a health disparity as a measurable difference in health that exists between specific population groups. This is a rigorously derived and data-driven determination operationalized by quantifiable metrics, rather than a statement of attribution. It is a scientific starting point that identifies where health outcomes diverge, not a predetermined conclusion about why. Scientific investigations to identify or understand the root causes are separate and distinct scientific questions, which are necessarily multifaceted and complex. NIH funded research is interested in those health disparities that are modifiable or actionable to improve the health of all population groups. Health disparities may be observed in the risks, prevalence, or problems resulting from specific behaviors, as well as the incidence, prevalence, and mortality from conditions, diseases, and/or disorders. To fulfill the NIH mission of seeking fundamental knowledge about the nature and behaviors of individuals as living systems, and the statutory purpose of NIMHD, to conduct research to understand and reduce health disparities, NIMHD Division of Intramural Research (DIR) conducts population health research to understand how health outcomes vary across populations, identify multilevel modifiable factors that drive these disparities, and develop, test, and evaluate clinical and population-based interventions to reduce these disparities. NIMHD DIR requires contractor assistance to provide R&D social and behavioral sciences research services to support NIMHD DIR in conducting population health and clinical research to understand and reduce health disparities in the United States. The Government anticipates that individual task orders may involve differing research designs, study populations, sites, durations, and levels of complexity. Interested firms should explain their ability to mobilize qualified personnel and research resources for multiple concurrent studies as requirements arise. NIMHD is seeking small businesses capable of designing, conducting and overseeing the clinical, scientific, and technical aspects of investigations into health disparities across populations, to identify modifiable risk and protective factors associated with these disparities, and develop and test interventions to reduce these disparities. Study designs to be used may include, but are not limited to: Population-based cross-sectional surveys; Epidemiological studies (e.g., longitudinal cohort study, case-control studies); Clinical trials; Community-based intervention studies; Simulation modeling; and Qualitative research methods (e.g., direct observations, in-depth interviews, focus groups discussions). Independently and not as an agent of the Government, the Contractor shall furnish all necessary services, qualified personnel, material, equipment, and facilities not otherwise provided by the Government to successfully perform the requirements stated below. Specifically, the Contractor shall, as required by individual task orders, perform the following technical requirements summarized below that also are included in the attached Draft Statement of Work (SOW), including but not limited to: Provide personnel, facilities, and other services necessary to maintain and coordinate multiple health disparities research studies funded through task orders under this Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract. Provide overall project management and coordination of activities performed under individual task orders, including development and maintenance of project plans, schedules, milestones, coordination of participating research sites and subcontractors, monitoring of performance, identification and resolution of project risks and issues, and preparation of progress reports as specified in the applicable task order. Conduct research studies through qualified organizations, as specified in individual task orders, and receiving consent from the Contracting Officer�s Representative (COR) and Contracting Officer (CO). This includes (but is not limited to) implementation of protocols; population health and clinical research site monitoring; regulatory compliance assurance; and analyses of data from clinical, laboratory, population and epidemiologic studies. title: France – Road transport services – 26SERV12 - Accord cadre à bons de commande pour les prestations de transport d'oeuvres et objets d'art pour les besoins de la Métropole Toulon Provence Méditerranée
description: Dans le cadre de sa politique culturelle, la Métropole Toulon Provence Méditerranée poursuit une politique d'attractivité territoriale en vue d'assurer un développement dynamique et durable et assume à ce titre la gestion en régie directe d'équipements culturels dans le domaine des arts visuels qui contribuent à son rayonnement au niveau national et international et dispose d'une collection d'oeuvres et objets d'art (art contemporain, photographie, sculptures). La présente consultation porte sur les besoins de la Métropole Toulon Provence Méditerranée en matière de prestations de transport d'oeuvres et objets d'art et activités connexes. Ces besoins concernent les oeuvres et objets d'art empruntés ou prêtés en France ou à l'étranger auprès d'acteurs publics et/ou privés (musées, institutions culturelles, galeries, collectionneurs...) pour la réalisation d'expositions temporaires ou dans le cadre de mouvements d'oeuvres. Ces prestations comprennent : - l'emballage des oeuvres et objets d'art avec étiquetage (du simple tamponnage à la fabrication et à la mise en caisse) aller/retour ; - les formalités « Beaux-arts » et douanières, - le transport des oeuvres et objets d'art par tout moyen (transport routier, aérien, maritime, fluvial ferroviaire) : l'acheminement depuis le ou les lieux d'enlèvement désignés (en France ou à l'étranger) vers les lieux de livraison désignés (en France ou à l'étranger) - les manutentions et le bardage (à savoir toutes formes de manutention manuelle ou mécanique pour déplacer et installer les oeuvres et objets d'art) à l'aller (avec une possible répartition dans les espaces des lieux désignés) et au retour, - le déballage des oeuvres et objets d'art à l'aller et au retour, - l'entreposage des oeuvres et objets d'art - des prestations complémentaires - le suivi et la coordination de ces différentes opérations.

title: Request for Information (RFI) for Aerial Targets Branch (EBAY) Air Force Aerial Target Solutions
description: Issued pursuant to Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) FAR 15.101(c) and RFO FAR Part 10 solely for information, market research, and planning purposes. This market survey is conducted by the Aerial Targets Program Office (AFLCMC/EBAY) under the Air Force Portfolio Acquisition Executive for Weapons (AFPAE/WP) to obtain industry capabilities, rough order of magnitude (ROM) information, and data needed to support commercial product/service, non-developmental item (NDI), and small business determinations under RFO FAR 10.001(f), and to inform acquisition planning. Per Title 10, U.S. Code �4172, major munitions and missile programs must demonstrate lethality against appropriate, threat-representative targets prior to full-rate production. The Aerial Targets mission is to provide target aircraft that replicate threat systems, including performance, signatures, and countermeasures of adversary aircraft. The objective of this RFI is to identify a range of solutions to populate a family for systems needed throughout the spectrum of missions in Defensive and Offensive Counter Air capabilities. These solutions may represent the full range of airborne threats, spanning from inexpensive �hobby drones� to the most advance adversary fighter and large-scale aircraft. This RFI is intended to: Identify commercially available or near-term solutions Understand industry capabilities and innovative approaches Inform future acquisition strategies and budgetary requirements and assist the agency in making commerciality, NDI, and small business set-aside determinations See attached RFI and Question and Answer documents and for additional details. ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ In accordance with Section 10 of the attached RFI, attached are the final Questions and Answers posted on 11 SEPTEMBER 2026. title: Request for Information (RFI) for Aerial Targets Branch (EBAY) Air Force Aerial Target Solutions
description: Issued pursuant to Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) FAR 15.101(c) and RFO FAR Part 10 solely for information, market research, and planning purposes. This market survey is conducted by the Aerial Targets Program Office (AFLCMC/EBAY) under the Air Force Portfolio Acquisition Executive for Weapons (AFPAE/WP) to obtain industry capabilities, rough order of magnitude (ROM) information, and data needed to support commercial product/service, non-developmental item (NDI), and small business determinations under RFO FAR 10.001(f), and to inform acquisition planning. Per Title 10, U.S. Code �4172, major munitions and missile programs must demonstrate lethality against appropriate, threat-representative targets prior to full-rate production. The Aerial Targets mission is to provide target aircraft that replicate threat systems, including performance, signatures, and countermeasures of adversary aircraft. The objective of this RFI is to identify a range of solutions to populate a family for systems needed throughout the spectrum of missions in Defensive and Offensive Counter Air capabilities. These solutions may represent the full range of airborne threats, spanning from inexpensive �hobby drones� to the most advance adversary fighter and large-scale aircraft. This RFI is intended to: Identify commercially available or near-term solutions Understand industry capabilities and innovative approaches Inform future acquisition strategies and budgetary requirements and assist the agency in making commerciality, NDI, and small business set-aside determinations See attached RFI and Question and Answer documents and for additional details. ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ In accordance with Section 10 of the attached RFI, attached are the final Questions and Answers posted on 11 SEPTEMBER 2026. description: This is a public notice prepared in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 5.2 � Synopsis of Proposed Contract Actions. The Library of Congress, Contracts and Grants Directorate, intends to award a sole-source firm fixed price contract to: SciAps, Inc (7 Constitution Way, Woburn, MA 01801-1194). title: Homeland Security and Innovation Center (HSIC) - Executive Education Seminar Services
description: HSIC, located at Joint Force Headquarters�Massachusetts, supports the National Guard by connecting senior-leader education with the evolving challenges of homeland security, emergency management, crisis leadership, and innovation. Its education mission includes General and Flag Officer Seminar (GFOS) and Leadership in Homeland Security (LHS) audiences. The seminars emphasize rigorous academic study, case-based analysis, facilitated discussion, critical thinking, and peer networking in a university setting. The curriculum should address National Guard roles in complex domestic response and intergovernmental coordination and, as appropriate to each seminar, emerging challenges such as artificial intelligence, cyber threats, small unmanned aircraft systems/counter-sUAS, and innovation. Inclusion and emphasis of these topics remain subject to HSIC/GOMO mission validation. The broader HSIC innovation/incubation mission does not automatically expand the scope of this seminar-services requirement. MARKET RESEARCH FEEDBACK REQUESTED Institutions are invited to comment on academic capability, delivery and pricing feasibility, and requirements that may unnecessarily constrain participation. Responses should identify the affected section, explain the practical or financial impact, and propose alternatives that preserve HSIC educational quality. Contracting will determine final response instructions. Academic institution and faculty qualifications: experience educating GOs or comparable senior executives; relevant faculty credentials; impact of tenured-Ph.D./ten-year criteria. GFOS and LHS differentiation: recommended objectives, topics, and approaches appropriate to each audience; capability to address AI, cyber, sUAS/cUAS, and innovation. Case-study pedagogy and research: existing course adaptation, case-study counts, original case development, guest speaker access, realistic research and approval timelines. Seminar capacity, location, and duration: in-person facilities for 65 plus support staff; viable course lengths; scheduling lead times; capacity for multiple annual iterations. Enrollment and pricing: ability to handle 40 Government-funded and up to 25 direct-pay seats; tuition-only versus standard bundled seminar pricing; minimum cohort sizes. Intellectual property: rights and restrictions for pre-existing materials versus Government-funded new case studies; possible licensing and reuse models. Participation barriers: federal contracting, administrative requirements, location, security, teaming, and any provisions that materially affect willingness or ability to compete. TARGETED UNIVERSITY FEEDBACK QUESTIONS � ACADEMIC AND BUSINESS FEASIBILITY Which performance outcomes and academic quality indicators best demonstrate that an executive education program meets HSIC needs? Which specific faculty criteria, if any, would prevent your institution from competing, and what evidence of equivalent academic quality could you provide? What case-study-based instructional model would you propose, and how would HSIC verify the quality of learning? What enrollment, lead time, and annual frequency would make participation financially viable for your institution? How would your institution price standard bundled tuition, meals, books, and facilities compared with a tuition-only arrangement, if available? Which administrative or payment requirements (including direct-pay seats and federal contracting) would discourage a response, and what alternatives could address them? Based on this draft PWS, what specific requirements or business conditions would discourage your institution from competing? Would your institution be interested in competing? If not, what changes would materially affect that decision? title: Request for Information (RFI) for Aerial Targets Branch (EBAY) Air Force Aerial Target Solutions
description: Issued pursuant to Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) FAR 15.101(c) and RFO FAR Part 10 solely for information, market research, and planning purposes. This market survey is conducted by the Aerial Targets Program Office (AFLCMC/EBAY) under the Air Force Portfolio Acquisition Executive for Weapons (AFPAE/WP) to obtain industry capabilities, rough order of magnitude (ROM) information, and data needed to support commercial product/service, non-developmental item (NDI), and small business determinations under RFO FAR 10.001(f), and to inform acquisition planning. Per Title 10, U.S. Code �4172, major munitions and missile programs must demonstrate lethality against appropriate, threat-representative targets prior to full-rate production. The Aerial Targets mission is to provide target aircraft that replicate threat systems, including performance, signatures, and countermeasures of adversary aircraft. The objective of this RFI is to identify a range of solutions to populate a family for systems needed throughout the spectrum of missions in Defensive and Offensive Counter Air capabilities. These solutions may represent the full range of airborne threats, spanning from inexpensive �hobby drones� to the most advance adversary fighter and large-scale aircraft. This RFI is intended to: Identify commercially available or near-term solutions Understand industry capabilities and innovative approaches Inform future acquisition strategies and budgetary requirements and assist the agency in making commerciality, NDI, and small business set-aside determinations See attached RFI and Question and Answer documents and for additional details. ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ In accordance with Section 10 of the attached RFI, attached are the final Questions and Answers posted on 11 SEPTEMBER 2026. title: Q301--NEW | Automated Blood Bank Solid Phase Analyzer and Associated Reagents/Consumables
description: This is a Sources Sought Notice NOT a Solicitation. Questions will NOT be answered. All responses should be submitted by November 25, 2026, at 1630 cst. Sources Sought Notice Automated Blood Bank Solid Phase Analyzer and Associated Reagents/Consumables to Rocky Mountain Regional VA Medical Center (RMRVAMC) Disclaimer: This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for market research information and planning purposes and does not constitute a solicitation. All information received in response to this RFI that is marked as proprietary will be handled accordingly. Responses to this notice are NOT offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Responders are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this RFI. Information Requested from Industry: In response to the Sources Sought, interested Contractors shall submit the following information and any Capabilities/Qualifications Statement to include but not limited to an overview of proposed solution(s) and a description of the product your company possesses in accordance with the Statement of Work draft / Salient Characteristics List. Responses to market research table questionnaire shall be submitted. If this information is not provided, then it will be assumed the entire requirement cannot be met. Description of Requirement: The Department of Veterans Affairs, Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Network Contracting Office 19 (NCO 19) is conducting a market survey and is seeking potential sources for an instrument rental reagent agreement for Automated Blood Bank Solid Phase Analyzer and Associated Reagents/Consumables for the Rocky Mountain Regional VA Medical Center. This Sources Sought Notice is issued for information and planning purposes only. This is not a solicitation or a request for proposal and shall not be construed as an obligation or commitment by the Government. An award will not be made on any offers submitted in response to this notice, and it shall not be implied that the Government is committed to providing any solicitation or award following this notice. The Government will not pay for any information received in response to this request, nor will the Government compensate a respondent for any costs incurred in developing the information provided. Period of Performance: 04/01/2027 through 03/31/2032 General Requirements: System must be new and in current production. Remanufactured and discontinued models are unacceptable. System must be capable of performing the following test on its solid phase automated analyzer: ABO/Rh Negative Rh Test reflexed to Weak D Antibody Screen, 3 cell screening panel required Antibody Identification of: Anti-E Anti-e Anti-C Anti-c Anti-K Anti-k Anti-D Anti-f Anti-Jka Anti-Jkb Anti-Fya Anti-Fyb Anti-M Anti-N Anti-S Anti-s Anti-P1 Anti-Lea Anti-Leb Anti-Lua Anti-Lub Antigen Phenotyping of: Anti-E Anti-e Anti-C Anti-c Anti-K Direct Antiglobulin Test (DAT) Crossmatching Donor Units with patient samples Ability to handle rouleaux, lipemic, icteric, and hemolyzed specimens. Define the actual hands-on maintenance time required for daily, weekly, monthly, and as needed maintenance. Contractor is to include the analyzer time required to perform each maintenance task and list which tasks are performed at the user level and which tasks are performed at the service level. Provide a comprehensive quality control (QC) program which includes the following options: QC files that can be edited or corrected for errors On-board quality control data storage and reporting capabilities DVD for data archive Ability to alert operator of QC failures Daily QC performance within 30 minutes System must be able to record and display temperature records. System must contain an automated cell washer with a wash cycle of less than 5 minutes and allows for processing of lipemic or icteric samples. System must have a centrifuge with automatic load/unload. System must contain a printer and necessary replacements and incubator capable of processing multiple runs simultaneously. The turnaround time for a Type & Screen shall be within 26 minutes. A monthly standing order for routine cell suspension reagents shall be provided. Reagents utilized for the analyzer must also be compatible with manual tube testing, which will serve as the backup testing method in the event of analyzer downtime. description: Die matrix Gesellschaft für Beratung in Wirtschaft, Politik und Verwaltung mbH & Co. KG führt im Auftrag des Ministeriums für Kultur und Wissenschaft des Landes Nordrhein-Westfalen die Landesgeschäftsstelle der Gemeinschaftsoffensive Zukunft durch Innovation.NRW (zdi.NRW). Sie schließt mit einem Unternehmen eine Rahmenvereinbarung über agile Softwareentwicklungsleistungen für die digitale zdi-Systemlandschaft mit dem Primärsystem mein.zdi.nrw. Gegenstand: Weiterentwicklung, Neuentwicklung, Integration, Migration, Wartung und Support sowie technische Betriebsunterstützung in einem verbindlichen Technologie-Stack (PHP und Symfony mit API Platform, Vue.js und Nuxt.js, PostgreSQL; Anbindung an Authentik, Airbyte, Apache Superset und Open WebUI). Die Leistungen werden über Leistungsfreigaben abgerufen, nach Aufwand zu festen Stundensätzen vergütet und grundsätzlich remote erbracht. Laufzeit und Umfang: ab Zuschlag, voraussichtlich Ende Dezember 2026; Leistungsfreigaben bis 31. Dezember 2030, Abwicklung bis 28. Februar 2031. Gesamthöchstwert 415.000 Euro netto ohne Mindestabnahme. Keine Aufteilung in Lose, keine Nebenangebote. Verfahren: Die Auftraggeberin ist keine öffentliche Auftraggeberin im Sinne von § 99 GWB. Sie führt das Verfahren freiwillig in Anlehnung an ein offenes Verfahren nach der VgV durch; maßgeblich sind die Vergabeunterlagen. Verhandlungen finden nicht statt. Ein Nachprüfungsverfahren vor der Vergabekammer findet nicht statt. Eignung: keine Ausschlussgründe (entsprechend §§ 123 und 124 GWB); Berufs- oder Betriebshaftpflichtversicherung mit mindestens 1.000.000 Euro je Schadensfall, auch für reine Vermögensschäden; mindestens zwei vergleichbare Referenzprojekte aus den letzten drei Jahren; Kernteam mit den Rollen Softwarearchitekt:in / Technical Lead, Senior Developer, Developer und DevOps / Systemintegration nach den Mindestanforderungen der Leistungsbeschreibung; sichere Kommunikation in deutscher Sprache; technische und organisatorische Maßnahmen nach Art. 32 DSGVO. Bietergemeinschaften sind zugelassen. Zuschlagskriterien: Bewertungspreis 40 Prozent, Qualität 60 Prozent (Entwicklungs- und Qualitätssicherungskonzept 20, Kernteam und technische Passung 15, Zusammenarbeit, Governance und Leistungsfreigaben 10, Effizienz, Automatisierung und KI-Integration 10, Wartung, Support, Dokumentation und Wissenstransfer 5). Datenschutz: Die Auftraggeberin verarbeitet die Daten der zdi-Systemlandschaft als Auftragsverarbeiterin des Landes Nordrhein-Westfalen; der Auftragnehmer wird weiterer Auftragsverarbeiter. Sein Einsatz setzt die Zustimmung des Landes voraus. Personen mit Zugriff auf personenbezogene Daten werden vor dem ersten Zugriff nach dem Verpflichtungsgesetz förmlich verpflichtet. Leistungen mit Zugriff auf personenbezogene Daten erbringen Beschäftigte des Auftragnehmers; Unterauftragnehmer und Unternehmen der Eignungsleihe erhalten keinen Zugriff auf solche Daten. Unterlagen und Fristen: Die Vergabeunterlagen stehen unter der in dieser Bekanntmachung angegebenen Internetadresse unentgeltlich, vollständig und ohne Registrierung zum Abruf bereit. Fragen bis Mittwoch, 25. November 2026. Angebotsfrist: Montag, 7. Dezember 2026, 10:00 Uhr. Bindefrist bis Freitag, 5. Februar 2027. Kommunikation, Fragen und Angebotsabgabe ausschließlich in Textform per E-Mail an zdi-ausschreibung@matrix-gruppe.de; Angebote in deutscher Sprache. Der Zuschlag wird nicht vor Ablauf von zehn Kalendertagen nach der Information der Bieter erteilt.

title: Germany – IT services: consulting, software development, Internet and support – NGA-Breitbandausbau-Spangenberg
description: Gegenstand dieser Ausschreibung ist die Beauftragung eines Unternehmens mit der Errichtung und dem Betrieb einer Gigabitinfrastruktur in den "grauen NGA-Gebieten" der Stadt Spangenberg. Das zu errichtende gigabitfähige Hochleistungsnetz muss eine Versorgung der im Ausbaugebiet ausgewiesenen Adressen mit einer Bandbreite von mindestens 1 Gbit/s symmetrisch (Mindestbandbreite) gewährleisten. Die Mindestbandbreite ist erreicht, wenn sie im Abschlusspunkt der Linientechnik im Gebäude bereitgestellt wird. Das durchgeführte Markterkundungsverfahren bestätigte, dass die Errichtung und der Betrieb eines solchen gigabitfähigen Hochleistungsnetzes im Ausbaugebiet nicht eigenwirtschaftlich abbildbar sind. Aus diesem Grund ist der Konzessionsgeber bereit, dem privaten Telekommunikationsunternehmen einen einmaligen, nicht rückzahlbaren Investitionszuschuss zur Deckung seiner Wirtschaftlichkeitslücke zur Verfügung zu stellen (sog. "Wirtschaftlichkeitslückenmodell"). Der Konzessionsgeber hat dazu im Rahmen des Förderprogramms des Bundes "Förderung zur Unterstützung des Gigabitausbaus der Telekommunikationsnetze in der Bundesrepublik Deutschland - Gigabit-Richtlinie 2.0" vom 13.01.2025 einen Förderantrag gestellt und Fördermittel in vorläufiger Höhe bewilligt bekommen.

title: Germany – Security services – Empfangs- und Sicherheitsdienstleistungen
description: Das Deutsche Institut für Ernährungsforschung Potsdam-Rehbrücke (DIfE) erforscht den Einfluss der Ernährung auf die Gesundheit, mit dem Ziel, wissenschaftliche Erkenntnisse für Prävention und Therapie ernährungsbedingter Erkrankungen nutzbar zu machen. Um neue Lösungsansätze aus dem Labor schnellstmöglich zum Menschen zu bringen, arbeiten die Wissenschaftlerinnen und Wissenschaftler in einer Kombination von experimenteller und angewandter Forschung: Von Zelle und Maus, über epidemiologische Beobachtungen, bis hin zu humanen Interventionen. Das DIfE beabsichtigt Empfangs- und Sicherungsdienstleistungen nach § 34a GewO und sicherungstechnische Überwachungsleistungen im Objektschutz gemäß nachfolgender Ausschreibung zum 21.02.2027 an einen externen Dienstleister zu vergeben. Dazu zählt die Prävention gegen alle Formen potentieller Angriffe insbesondere auf die Objekte und ihren Inhalt, das Eigentum und Vermögen mit Intervention bei Alarmmeldungen sowie sonstigen Vorkommnissen. An die interne und externe Intervention werden besondere qualitative Ansprüche gestellt.

title: Sweden – Financial analysis software package – ALM System and Services
description: The Swedish National Debt Office (Riksgälden), hereinafter referred to as “SNDO”, requires an Asset and Liability Management (ALM) system and related services, including software licences or subscriptions, implementation, operation, maintenance, support, training and consultancy services, hereinafter collectively referred to as the “ALM System and Services”. The ALM System will be used to perform asset and liability management analyses relating to the system for financing nuclear decommissioning and waste management in Sweden, hereinafter referred to as the “Financing System”. The primary purposes of the analyses are to: a) assess the risk that the assets and future income of the Financing System will be insufficient to meet its future liabilities, including the calculation and analysis of the Risk Margin; and b) support decisions concerning the strategic asset allocation of the Nuclear Waste Fund. The Agreement will enter into force when it has been signed by both parties, which is expected to occur in December 2026. Implementation, model configuration, testing and other activities required for production deployment shall commence following the entry into force of the Agreement. The ALM System shall be approved and ready for production use no later than 1 January 2027. The operational services period will commence on 1 January 2027. The initial operational services period will be three (3) years. Thereafter, the Agreement will be automatically extended for successive periods of one (1) year at a time, unless terminated by SNDO in accordance with the Agreement. The maximum operational services period, including all extensions, is eight (8) years. The procurement is not divided into separate lots. For organisational, functional and risk-related reasons, SNDO requires the ALM System and Services to be provided as a single, integrated delivery. The assignment requires the Supplier to assume overall responsibility for the implementation, functionality, operation, support and maintenance of the ALM System and for the coordination of the related services throughout the contract period. Dividing the procurement into separate lots would make it more difficult to ensure coherent functionality, clear allocation of responsibility and effective implementation and operation. SNDO therefore considers that dividing the procurement into separate lots would not be appropriate.

title: Netherlands – Energy-efficiency consultancy services – Onderzoek/verkenning energiegemeenschappen
description: De gemeenten Bergeijk, Bladel, Eersel, Oirschot en Reusel-De Mierden (hierna: aanbestedende dienst of opdrachtgever) besteden deze opdracht in gezamenlijkheid aan. Bizob treedt op als aanbestedende dienst voor deze aanbesteding namens alle hiervoor genoemde organisaties. De opdracht heeft in eerste instantie betrekking op de uitvoering van de externe verkenning, aangeduid als fase 2. De beoogde ingangsdatum van de overeenkomst is 1 maart 2027. Omdat de opdracht op basis van een hybride specificatie (functionele eisen aangevuld met technische uitvoeringsvoorwaarden) in de markt wordt gezet (zie hoofdstuk 2), kent de overeenkomst geen vaste looptijd. Het betreft een eenmalige, resultaatgerichte dienstverlening die uiterlijk binnen 12 maanden na start wordt afgerond, waarbij geldt dat het eindresultaat formeel door de individuele opdrachtgever dient te zijn geaccepteerd. Beoogd wordt dat het op te leveren eindproduct uiterlijk medio januari 2028 gereed is voor bestuurlijke besluitvorming. Afhankelijk van het resultaat van fase 2 en de besluitvorming hieromtrent door opdrachtgever, kan per individuele gemeente besloten worden tot opdrachtverstrekking voor de optionele vervolgfase (fase 3). Deze fase ziet op de ondersteuning bij de verdere uitwerking en realisatie van initiatieven en energiegemeenschappen. De uitvoering van deze fase is voorzien in de periode vanaf 1 februari 2028 tot en met een nader te bepalen einddatum. De daadwerkelijke doorlooptijd van fase 3 is afhankelijk van verschillende factoren, waaronder de uitkomsten van de externe verkenning, de aard en kenmerken van de initiatieven en de benodigde bestuurlijke besluitvorming. Het tempo en de fasering van de uitvoering kunnen hierdoor per initiatief en gemeente, verschillen.

title: Supply Chain Notice - WC2126918 - XSP513 - Refurbishment of Sports Facility (Running Track), Dhekelia, CYPRUS
description: - Clean surface of existing asphalt track and prepare surface to receive new synthetic poroplastic layer. Repair and seal any cracks found following the cleaning process using cold applied plastic MMA which is a highly durable, two component material formulated from methyl methacrylate resin and a chemical catalyst. - Replace sections of the drainage channel along the inner perimeter of the running track where necessary. Additionally, remove all accumulated debris, thoroughly clean the en-tire drainage channel using high-pressure water jetting, and ensure that the drainage outlets are clear and functioning properly to allow unrestricted water discharge. - Replace damaged or deteriorated sections of the soft kerbing along the outer perimeter of the running track, wherever necessary, ensuring proper alignment, secure installation and a consistent finish. - Lay new synthetic surface "PoplasticSW competition" or equivalent, consisting of 10-12mm elastic layer laid on the asphalt subbase, pore sealing and finish with structural cast coating 3-5mm thick. - Provide new markings for the running track in compliance with World Athletics (formerly IAAF) regulations. The Provisional Key Tender dates for the project are as follows: - Expression of interest: 13/11/2026 - Expression of interest return: 25/11/2026 - Invitation to Tender: 30/11/2026 - Tender Return Date: 08/01/2027 - Contract award: 15/02/2027 - Commencement of work: 22/02/2027 - Completion of work: 30/06/2027 The currency of this project is Euro (€). The location of this project is Dhekelia, Cyprus (British Forces). Additional information: Any company wishing to participate in this tender should complete the Pre-Qualification Questionnaire (PQQ) and the EOI form which are attached and return them electronically to the above email address by no later than 12:00 EET on 25/11/2026. For companies that have submitted a PQQ within the last 12 months, there is no requirement to re-submit it. They must provide the details of their last PQQ submission to guarantee inclusion on the invitation list.
